definition_zh: 选择；选项；选择权；（金融）期权；（计算机）选项
definition_en: one of several things that can be chosen; the freedom or right to choose; a right to buy or sell something at a fixed price
core_image: 几张摊开的牌，你伸手只拿起其中一张
scene: 申请研究生时，她在纸上列出三所学校，比较学费、城市和专业方向。She wrote: Each school is one option, and I can keep all three open until the last week.
sceneCN: 这里 option 是「可供选择的方案」（第 1 个义项：可选的事物之一）；句意：每一所学校都是一个选项，我可以把这三所学校都留到最后一刻再决定。图中可辨识物件：申请表、三所学校名单、铅笔、计算器。

pos.zh: 选择；选项；可选择的事物

collocations.zh: 保留选择余地；不急于定死

senses.title: One of the things you can choose
senses.definition: one of two or more things that you can choose to have or do
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个可供选择的事物中的一个
senses.example: Studying abroad is one option; staying at home is another.
senses.exampleCN: 出国留学是一种选择，留在国内是另一种选择。
senses.why: The word names the item sitting in front of the chooser. Latin optio meant 'choice' as an act; by 1885 English extended it to 'the thing that may be chosen', so the abstract act became a concrete item on a list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指“选择”这个行为，后来指摆在选择者面前的那一项。拉丁语 optio 是“选择”；英语到 1885 年才把它扩展到“可供选择的事物”，抽象行为于是变成了清单上的具体一项。

senses.title: The freedom or right to choose
senses.definition: the power or liberty of choosing, especially when nothing is forced
senses.definitionCN: 选择的能力或自由，尤指没有被强迫时
senses.example: Employees have the option of working from home two days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 员工可以选择每周有两天在家办公。
senses.why: From c. 1600 'action of choosing' came the 1630s sense 'power or liberty of choosing'. The emphasis moves from the chosen item to the chooser's open hand: what matters is that the hand is not forced.
senses.whyCN: 从 1600 年前后的“选择行为”，发展出 1630 年代的“选择权、选择自由”。重点从被选的物件移到了选择者那只未被强迫的手。

senses.title: An extra feature you may add
senses.titleCN: 可选配置：加钱才有的附加功能
senses.definition: a feature or piece of equipment that is available only if the buyer chooses and usually pays for it
senses.definitionCN: 只有买家选择并通常额外付费才提供的功能或设备
senses.example: Air conditioning is an option on this model, not standard equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 空调是这款车型的选装配置，不是标配。
senses.why: Here the choice itself is turned into a product. The buyer's open hand is priced: you may take the extra feature or leave it, and either way the base item still works.
senses.whyCN: 这里被出售的正是“选择”本身。选择者那只张开的手被标上了价格：你可以拿这项附加功能，也可以不拿，而基础产品照样能用。

senses.title: Stock option: a right to buy shares
senses.titleCN: 股票期权：按约定价格买股份的权利
senses.definition: a right given to an employee or investor to buy company shares at a set price within a set period
senses.definitionCN: 给予员工或投资者在约定期限内按约定价格购买公司股份的权利
senses.example: The startup offered her stock options as part of the package.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司把股票期权作为薪酬方案的一部分提供给她。
senses.why: A share option is literally a purchased choice: the holder may buy at the fixed price or walk away. The 1755 commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium' is the direct ancestor of this financial use.
senses.whyCN: 股票期权字面上就是“买来的选择权”：持有人可以按固定价格买入，也可以放弃。1755 年那条“支付权利金换得的特权”的商业义，正是这一金融用法的直系祖先。

senses.title: Option contract: a right with a price
senses.titleCN: 期权合约：有价格的权利
senses.definition: a contract giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a stated price before a deadline
senses.definitionCN: 赋予买方在截止日期前按约定价格买入或卖出资产的权利而非义务的合约
senses.example: The fund bought an option to purchase the land at a fixed price.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金买入了按固定价格购买这块土地的选择权。
senses.why: The legal instrument isolates the core idea of the word: a choice that is bought, bounded by a price and a date. The holder pays for the open hand and may still refuse to close it.
senses.whyCN: 这种法律工具把词的核心抽离出来：一个被买下、受价格和日期约束的选择。持有人为那只张开的手付费，并且仍然可以拒绝合拢。

senses.title: The option play in football
senses.titleCN: 美式橄榄球中的“选择战术”
senses.definition: an American football play in which the ball carrier may either pass or run
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球中持球者可选择传球或自己带球推进的战术
senses.example: The quarterback kept the ball on the option play.
senses.exampleCN: 四分卫在这个选择战术中自己带球推进。
senses.why: Recorded by 1953, the play gives the carrier two live choices at the moment of action. The name is not about a product or a contract but about a decision still open while the body is already moving.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法记录于 1953 年：战术让持球者在动作发生的瞬间保有两条真实可走的路线。名字说的不是产品或合约，而是身体已经动起来时仍然敞开的选择。

senses.title: A setting or flag in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的选项或参数开关
senses.definition: a selectable setting, flag, or argument that changes how a program behaves
senses.definitionCN: 改变程序行为方式的可选设置、开关或参数
senses.example: Add the -v option to see verbose output.
senses.exampleCN: 加上 -v 选项即可查看详细输出。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the everyday sense: a program offers a menu of behaviours, and the user picks one. The choice is now made by typing a flag rather than by pointing at a card.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了日常义：程序把若干行为列成菜单，用户挑一个。选择方式从“指着卡片”变成了“敲一个参数”。

senses.title: Keeping alternatives available
senses.titleCN: 保留余地：让选择继续敞开
senses.definition: in the phrase keep options open, to avoid committing so that alternatives stay available
senses.definitionCN: 用于 keep options open，表示不做出承诺，以便保留其他可能
senses.example: She kept her options open by applying to several programs.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了好几个项目，以此保留选择余地。
senses.why: This phrase makes the open hand visible. Not choosing yet is itself a choice, because the alternatives remain graspable and no single card has been lifted from the table.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让“张开的手”变得可见。暂不选择本身也是一种选择：其他可能仍然可抓，桌上没有哪张牌被真正拿走。

intro.en: Option comes from Latin through French. The date of the English noun is clear; the origin of the Latin verb optare is not, and standard references mark it as uncertain.
intro.cn: option 经由法语来自拉丁语。英语名词的年代清楚，但拉丁动词 optare 的来源并不清楚，通行资料标注为不确定。

items.en: c. 1600, 'action of choosing'; by the 1630s, 'power or liberty of choosing'. The noun entered English through French option (Old French opcion).
items.cn: 约 1600 年记录为“选择的行为”；到 1630 年代为“选择的能力或自由”。名词经法语 option（古法语 opcion）进入英语。

items.en: From Latin optionem (nominative optio) 'choice, free choice, liberty to choose', a noun from optare 'to desire, pray for, choose'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 optionem（主格 optio）“选择、自由选择、选择的自由”，是由 optare“渴望、祈求、选择”构成的名词。

items.en: De Vaan derives optare from Proto-Italic *opeje- 'to choose, grab', from PIE *hopeie-, and compares Hittite epp-/app- 'to take, grab'. This deeper reconstruction is debated, so the ultimate root is source uncertain.
items.cn: De Vaan 把 optare 追溯到原始意大利语 *opeje-“选择、抓取”，再往上到原始印欧语 *hopeie-，并与赫梯语 epp-/app-“拿、抓”比较。这一更深层重构仍有争议，故最底层词源来源不确定。

items.en: 1755 records the commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium'; 1885 records 'thing that may be chosen'. The word thus moved from act to right to object.
items.cn: 1755 年记录商业义“支付权利金换得的特权”；1885 年记录“可供选择的事物”。词义由此从行为走到权利，再走到物件。

items.en: 1953 records the football option play. The computing sense of a selectable flag is a later 20c. extension of the everyday 'choice' meaning.
items.cn: 1953 年记录橄榄球的 option play（选择战术）。计算机中“可选开关”的义项是 20 世纪后期由日常“选择”义扩展而来。

note.en: The first group separates words that merely look like option; the second compares words that really mean a choice.
note.cn: 第一组只把外形相近的词分开；第二组比较真正表示“选择”的词。

entries.definition: a process or set of actions, especially in surgery or business. It starts with op- but comes from Latin opus 'work', not optare.
entries.definitionCN: 操作；手术；业务。它同样以 op- 开头，但来自拉丁语 opus“工作”，而不是 optare。

entries.definition: a belief or judgment not fully proved. It is linked in dictionaries to opinari 'to think', whose own origin is unknown, and is not a form of option.
entries.definitionCN: 意见；看法。词典把它连到 opinari“认为”，而 opinari 本身来源不明，它不是 option 的变形。

entries.definition: relating to light or the eyes. Its opt- goes back to Greek optos 'seen', a different root from Latin optare.
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；视觉的。它的 opt- 来自希腊语 optos“被看见的”，与拉丁语 optare 是不同的词根。

entries.definition: in grammar, a mood that expresses a wish. It is built directly on Latin optare 'to wish', so it is a true relative of option.
entries.definitionCN: 语法中的祈愿语气。它直接由拉丁语 optare“希望”构成，因此是 option 的真正同族词。

entries.definition: the act of choosing, or the range of things from which one may choose. It is the everyday word; option is more formal and often implies a listed alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 选择的行为，或可供选择的整体范围。它是最日常的词；option 更正式，常指清单上列出的一个备选。

entries.definition: one of two or more possibilities that can replace each other. It stresses replacement; option stresses that the thing is available to pick.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或多个可相互替代的可能之一。它强调“替换”，option 强调“可供挑选”。

entries.definition: the act of selecting, or the set of things chosen. It often refers to a curated range rather than a single item.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的行为，或被挑出的一组事物。它常指经过整理的一组，而不是单个选项。

entries.definition: a stronger liking for one thing over another. It names the ranking in the chooser's mind, not the item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物更强的偏好。它指选择者心里的排序，而不是被选的那个事物。

normalIntro.en: Five sound-and-spelling hooks, then three abstract images for the idea behind the word.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个读音与拼写挂钩，再用三个抽象画面记住这个词背后的观念。

normal.en: op- sounds like 'open': an option is a door left open until you walk through one.
normal.cn: op- 听起来像 open（打开）：option 就是一扇直到你走进某一间之前都开着的门。

normal.en: -tion marks an action, as in action: choosing is something you do, not a thing that happens to you.
normal.cn: -tion 像 action 里的那个 -tion，标记“动作”：选择是你做的事，不是落到你身上的事。

normal.en: opt out is 'choose out', opt in is 'choose in': the same root with opposite directions.
normal.cn: opt out 是“选出去”（退出），opt in 是“选进来”（加入）：同一个词根，方向相反。

normal.en: Keep options open = keep the cards on the table, not in your pocket.
normal.cn: keep options open＝把牌留在桌上，而不是揣进口袋。

normal.en: optional ends in -al like 'additional': an optional extra is one you may add.
normal.cn: optional 和 additional 一样以 -al 结尾：optional extra 就是你可以“加”的那一项。

abstract.en: An option is the smallest unit of freedom: a real alternative that you can still take.
abstract.cn: 选项是自由的最小单位：一个你仍然拿得走的真实备选。

abstract.en: Every option is a road not yet walked; choosing burns the other roads for this trip.
abstract.cn: 每个选项都是一条尚未走过的路；一旦选择，这一趟的其他路就被烧掉了。

abstract.en: A financial option puts a price on possibility itself: you pay to keep a choice alive.
abstract.cn: 金融期权给“可能性”本身标了价：你付钱，只为让一个选择继续活着。

examples.en: The report lists several options for cutting costs, but none is painless.
examples.cn: 报告列出了几种削减成本的选项，但没有一种是轻松的。

examples.en: You always have the option to say no.
examples.cn: 你始终拥有拒绝的选项。

examples.en: The software hides advanced options unless you open the settings panel.
examples.cn: 除非打开设置面板，否则软件会隐藏高级选项。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 opt- 记成“伸手抓取”，-ion 记成“动作”：抓取的动作就是选择。
dict_mnemonic.text: opt（抓取、选择）+ -ion（名词）→ 选择、选项、选择权

root: 拉丁 optare“希望、选择”→ optio“选择”→ 法语 option → 英语 option；更早的原始印欧来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from 'a thing you may pick' to 'the right to pick', then to priced choices (features, stock, contracts), and finally to a live choice inside a game, a program, or a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“可供挑选的事物”走到“挑选的权利”，再到被标价的选择（选装配置、股票、合约），最后落到比赛、程序与计划中仍然敞开的那一次选择。

core.en: An open hand above several alternatives, ready to lift one
core.cn: 悬在几个备选之上的手，随时准备拿起一个

branches.en: Concrete alternatives: one item on a list of things you may pick.
branches.cn: 具体备选：可供挑选的清单上的一项。

branches.en: Freedom kept open: the chooser's liberty, or the deliberate refusal to commit.
branches.cn: 被保留的自由：选择者的权利，或有意不作承诺。

branches.en: Choices sold as goods: an add-on feature or a stock option.
branches.cn: 作为商品出售的选择：选装配置或股票期权。

branches.en: Choices inside a system: a football play or a software flag.
branches.cn: 系统内部的选择：橄榄球战术或软件开关。

branches.en: The paid right: liberty turned into a priced, time-limited contract.
branches.cn: 付费的权利：自由变成有价格、有期限的合约。

intro.en: The opt- family is small but busy: a verb of choosing, a noun of choice, and adjectives that mark whether something is left to the chooser.
intro.cn: opt- 词族不大但很活跃：一个“选择”动词、一个“选择”名词，以及标记“是否交由选择者决定”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin optare 'to wish, choose' yields optio 'choice' and the adjective optativus 'expressing a wish'. English opt is a back-formation from option.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optare“希望、选择”产生 optio“选择”和形容词 optativus“表达愿望的”。英语的 opt 是从 option 逆构出来的动词。

items.meaning: the act or right of choosing; a thing chosen
items.meaningCN: 选择的行为或权利；被选中的事物
items.example: You have the option to decline.
items.exampleCN: 你有权拒绝。

items.meaning: left to choice, not required
items.example: Attendance is optional.
items.exampleCN: 出席与否是自愿的。

items.meaning: in a way that is not required
items.example: The form can optionally include a photo.
items.exampleCN: 表格可以选择附上一张照片。

items.meaning: to choose or decide between alternatives
items.example: Most students opt for the shorter course.
items.exampleCN: 大多数学生选择较短的那门课。

items.meaning: a choice to leave or not take part
items.example: The newsletter uses an opt-out system.
items.exampleCN: 这份通讯采用“默认订阅、可退出”的机制。

items.meaning: a choice to join or take part
items.example: Marketing emails require opt-in consent.
items.exampleCN: 营销邮件需要用户主动选择加入的同意。

items.meaning: to choose for oneself and take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 采纳；收养（选择过来成为自己的）
items.example: The school adopted a new reading method.
items.exampleCN: 学校采纳了一种新的阅读教学法。

items.meaning: the act of taking something as one's own
items.example: The adoption of the plan took two years.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划的采纳用了两年。

items.meaning: expressing a wish, as a grammatical mood
items.example: Ancient Greek has an optative mood.
items.exampleCN: 古希腊语有祈愿语气。

latinEntries.example: Latin optare aliquid means to wish for something.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 optare aliquid 意为“渴望某物”。

latinEntries.meaning: choice, free choice, liberty to choose
latinEntries.meaningCN: 选择、自由选择、选择的自由
latinEntries.example: Optio is the source of French option.
latinEntries.exampleCN: optio 是法语 option 的来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to choose for oneself, take by choice
latinEntries.meaningCN: 为自己挑选；选择并接纳
latinEntries.example: Adoptare is the source of English adopt.
latinEntries.exampleCN: adoptare 是英语 adopt 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Optativus modus is the wishing mood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: optativus modus 即祈愿语气。

definition_zh: 东方；日出方向；使朝向；确定方位；使适应
definition_en: the east or the eastern world; to place something in relation to the compass, or to adjust oneself to a new situation
core_image: 罗盘针稳稳指向太阳升起的那一边
scene: 新生报到那天，她站在校园地图前先找北。She turned the map until the buildings matched the ground, and that was enough to orient herself.
sceneCN: 这里 orient 是“确定方位、使自己适应环境”（第 6 个义项：在新环境中找到自己的位置）；句意：她把地图转到与地面建筑对齐，这样就足以让自己确定方位。图中可辨识物件：校园地图、指南针、宿舍楼、图书馆、教学楼。

pos.zh: 东方；东方国家（常大写 Orient）
日出方向；地平线上的东点
使朝向；确定方位；使适应

collocations.zh: 确定自己的方位；使自己适应
使某物朝向；使某物以……为目标
东方（常指东亚及中东，带历史色彩）

derivatives.zh: 方向；定位；入学导览；取向
东方的（现常被视为带殖民色彩，慎用）

senses.title: The east as a region
senses.definition: the eastern part of the world, especially Asia and the Middle East, often written with a capital O
senses.definitionCN: 世界的东部，尤指亚洲与中东，常大写为 Orient
senses.example: Spices reached Europe from the Orient by sea.
senses.exampleCN: 香料经海路从东方运抵欧洲。
senses.why: Latin oriens meant 'the rising sun' and then 'the part of the sky where the sun rises', and from that 'the lands in that direction'. A region is named by the daily event that marks its side of the horizon.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 oriens 先指“正在升起的太阳”，再指“太阳升起的那片天空”，最后指“那个方向的土地”。一个区域，是用每天发生在那一侧地平线上的事件来命名的。

senses.title: The direction of sunrise
senses.definition: the east, or the point on the horizon where the sun first appears
senses.definitionCN: 东方，或地平线上太阳最初出现的那一点
senses.example: The wall faces orient, so it catches the first light.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙朝东，因此能接住清晨第一缕光。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: orient as a direction rather than a culture. The word is a compass point before it is a place, because the rising sun is the most reliable daily marker of east.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：orient 是方向，而不是文化。它先是罗盘上的一个点，然后才是一个地方，因为升起的太阳是“东”最可靠的每日标记。

senses.title: The luster of a fine pearl
senses.definition: the delicate iridescence of a fine pearl, formerly called its orient
senses.definitionCN: 上等珍珠那种柔和而变幻的光泽，旧称 orient
senses.example: The necklace was valued for the orient of its pearls.
senses.exampleCN: 这条项链因珍珠的光泽而昂贵。
senses.why: A 'pearl of the Orient' originally meant a pearl from the Indian seas; by 1755 the phrase had shortened into a name for the pearl's own sheen. The east became a quality of light.
senses.whyCN: “东方珍珠”原指来自印度洋的珍珠；到 1755 年，这个短语缩略成了珍珠自身光泽的名称。东方由此变成了一种光的质地。

senses.title: To face something eastward
senses.definition: to arrange or build something so that it faces east
senses.definitionCN: 把某物布置或建造得面向东方
senses.example: The chapel was oriented so the altar faced the sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 礼拜堂被布置成祭坛朝向日出的方向。
senses.why: The verb entered in 1738 from French s'orienter, literally 'to face east'. Church builders used the sunrise as a fixed reference, so the act of turning east became a general verb of placing.
senses.whyCN: 动词 1738 年经法语 s'orienter 进入英语，字面就是“面朝东方”。教堂建造者把日出当作固定参照，于是“转向东方”这个动作变成了通用的“定位”动词。

senses.title: To align with the compass
senses.definition: to place or adjust something in a definite position relative to north, south, east and west
senses.definitionCN: 使某物相对于东南西北处于一个确定的位置
senses.example: Orienting the map north made the trail easy to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 把地图按北向摆正后，小路就容易辨认了。
senses.why: By 1842 the east-facing act was generalized to any compass direction. The original eastward bias disappears, but the structure stays: a fixed frame outside you decides how things are placed.
senses.whyCN: 到 1842 年，“面朝东”的动作被推广到任何方位。原本偏东的倾向消失了，但结构仍在：由你之外的一个固定框架来决定事物怎么摆放。

senses.title: To get your bearings in a new situation
senses.titleCN: 在新环境中找到自己的位置
senses.definition: to make yourself familiar with a new place, situation, or set of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 使自己熟悉新的地点、处境或一套观念
senses.example: New students spend the first week orienting themselves to campus life.
senses.exampleCN: 新生用第一周时间适应校园生活、找准自己的位置。
senses.why: The figurative sense is recorded by 1850. If facing east let a traveler know where he stood, then understanding a new situation is the same operation carried out with ideas instead of landmarks.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义记录于 1850 年。既然“面朝东”能让旅人知道自己身在何处，那么理解一个新处境就是同一套操作，只不过用观念代替了地标。

senses.title: To aim something toward a purpose
senses.titleCN: 使某物以某个目的为导向
senses.definition: to design or direct something so that it serves a particular group or goal
senses.definitionCN: 把某物设计或引导得服务于特定群体或目标
senses.example: The program is oriented towards first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目是面向一年级学生的。
senses.why: Once orient means 'place relative to a frame', the frame can be a goal rather than a compass. The thing is turned so that its front faces the purpose, and everything else is arranged behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 orient 表示“相对于某个框架摆放”，这个框架就可以是目标而不是罗盘。事物被转得正面朝向目的，其余部分则排在它后面。

senses.title: Archaic: eastern or rising
senses.definition: in older or poetic use, eastern, or (of the sun) rising
senses.definitionCN: 在较古或诗歌用法中，指东方的，或（太阳）正在升起的
senses.example: The orient sun lit the top of the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 初升的太阳照亮了神庙顶端。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the original participle meaning of oriens, 'rising'. Modern English mostly replaced it with eastern, leaving orient as a poetic echo of the moment the sun clears the horizon.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了 oriens 最初的分词义“正在升起”。现代英语大多用 eastern 取代了它，只把 orient 留作太阳越过地平线那一刻的诗意回声。

intro.en: Orient is a Latin participle that became a place, a direction, a verb, and a quality of pearls. The chain back to oriri 'to rise' is firm; the PIE root is reconstructed but well supported.
intro.cn: orient 是一个拉丁语分词，先后变成地名、方向、动词和珍珠的质感。追溯到 oriri“升起”这条链是可靠的；原始印欧词根为重构形式，但证据充分。

items.en: The noun appears meaning 'the direction east; the part of the horizon where the sun first appears', and also 'the eastern regions of the world'.
items.cn: 名词出现，义为“东方；太阳最初出现的那段地平线”，也指“世界东部地区”。

items.en: From Old French orient 'east' (11c.), from Latin orientem (nominative oriens) 'the rising sun, the east'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 orient“东方”（11 世纪），再来自拉丁语 orientem（主格 oriens）“升起的太阳、东方”。

items.en: Oriens is the present participle of oriri 'to rise, get up, appear above the horizon, be born'. The same verb gives origin and original.
items.cn: oriens 是 oriri“升起、起身、出现在地平线上、出生”的现在分词。同一个动词还产生 origin 与 original。

items.en: Oriri is traced to PIE *heri- 'to rise', source also of Hittite arai- 'to arise, lift'. The reconstruction is standard, though the asterisk marks it as reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: oriri 被追溯到原始印欧语 *heri-“升起”，也是赫梯语 arai-“升起、举起”的来源。该重构属通行说法，星号表示它是重构而非实际记录的词形。

items.en: 1738 brings the verb, from French s'orienter 'to take one's bearings'; 1842 extends it to any compass position; 1850 records the figurative 'adjust to a new situation'.
items.cn: 1738 年经法语 s'orienter“辨认方位”引入动词；1842 年扩展到任何罗盘方位；1850 年记录“适应新处境”的比喻义。

note.en: Look-alikes here are mostly family members; the near-meaning group separates the compass word from words about adapting.
note.cn: 这里的形近词多是同族词；近义组则把“方位”词与“适应”类词分开。

entries.definition: of or from the East. It is the adjective from orient, now often avoided because of its colonial history.
entries.definitionCN: 东方的；来自东方的。它是 orient 的形容词，因殖民历史如今常被回避。

entries.definition: the act of finding direction, or the direction something faces; also an introductory program.
entries.definitionCN: 确定方向的行为，或某物朝向的方向；也指入学导览。

entries.definition: the beginning or source of something. It comes from the same oriri 'to rise', but names a starting point rather than an eastern direction.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的起点或来源。它来自同一个 oriri“升起”，但指起点，而不是东方。

entries.definition: the West. It is built on occidere 'to fall', the mirror image of oriri 'to rise', so east and west are named by sunrise and sunset.
entries.definitionCN: 西方。它由 occidere“落下”构成，与 oriri“升起”正好镜像：东西方是用日出与日落命名的。

entries.definition: the compass direction of sunrise. It is the plain everyday word; orient is the formal or literary name for the same direction or region.
entries.definitionCN: 日出的罗盘方向。它是最朴素的日常词；orient 是同一方向或区域的正式、文学说法。

entries.definition: located in or coming from the east. It is the neutral adjective that has largely replaced orient in everyday use.
entries.definitionCN: 位于东方或来自东方的。它是中性的形容词，在日常用法中已基本取代 orient。

entries.definition: to place things in a straight line or in correct relative position. It stresses the line; orient stresses the reference frame.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物排成直线或摆到正确的相对位置。它强调“线”，orient 强调“参照框架”。

entries.definition: to change oneself to fit new conditions. It is broader than orient oneself, which is specifically about finding one's place first.
entries.definitionCN: 改变自己以适应新条件。它比 orient oneself 更宽，后者特指先找到自己的位置。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the spelling, then three abstract images built on the sunrise.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个拼写钩子，再用三个围绕日出的抽象画面。

normal.en: ori- is the sound of 'rise' in origin: both come from oriri, to rise.
normal.cn: ori- 听起来像 origin 里的“升起”：两者都来自 oriri（升起）。

normal.en: Orient and Occident are twins: the sun rises in the east and falls in the west.
normal.cn: Orient 与 Occident 是一对双胞胎：太阳在东边升起，在西边落下。

normal.en: orientation week is literally the week you learn which way is which.
normal.cn: orientation week（入学导览周）字面上就是“学会哪边是哪边”的那一周。

normal.en: disorient = dis- (away) + orient: to take the east, and the bearings, away from you.
normal.cn: disorient＝dis-（离开）+ orient：把东方、也把你的方位感拿走。

normal.en: oriented ends in -ed like 'pointed': something oriented is pointed at a target.
normal.cn: oriented 和 pointed 一样以 -ed 结尾：oriented 的东西是被“指”向某个目标的。

abstract.en: East is not a place but an event: the daily moment the sun clears the edge of the world.
abstract.cn: 东方不是一个地点，而是一个事件：太阳每天越过世界边缘的那一刻。

abstract.en: To orient yourself is to admit that you need a frame larger than your own body.
abstract.cn: 确定方位，就是承认自己需要一个比身体更大的框架。

abstract.en: Every culture that names itself after sunrise is quietly placing itself at the centre of the map.
abstract.cn: 每个以日出命名自己的文化，都在悄悄把自己放在地图的中心。

examples.en: The trade routes of the Orient carried silk, spices, and ideas.
examples.cn: 东方贸易路线运送丝绸、香料与思想。

examples.en: She oriented the telescope toward the eastern horizon.
examples.cn: 她把望远镜朝向东方地平线。

examples.en: It took him a month to orient himself in the new lab.
examples.cn: 他花了一个月才在新实验室里找准自己的位置。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 orient 记成“太阳升起的那一边”，再引申为“朝着那边摆正”。
dict_mnemonic.text: oriens（升起的太阳）→ orient（东方；使朝向）

root: 拉丁 oriri“升起”→ oriens“升起的（太阳）、东方”→ 法语 orient → 英语 orient；同族有 origin、original、abort。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a region named after sunrise, to the compass point, to a pearl's sheen, and then to the act of turning something toward a reference and finally toward a goal.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“以日出命名的区域”走到罗盘方位，再到珍珠的光泽，最后落到“把某物转向参照系、再转向目标”的动作。

core.en: A compass needle holding steady toward the sunrise
core.cn: 罗盘针稳稳指向日出的方向

branches.en: The place and the direction: where the sun comes up, and the lands on that side.
branches.cn: 地点与方向：太阳升起之处，以及那一侧的土地。

branches.en: Light as a quality: the east becomes the shimmer inside a pearl.
branches.cn: 光作为质地：东方变成珍珠内部的闪色。

branches.en: Physical placement: face east, then face any fixed compass point.
branches.cn: 物理摆放：先面朝东，再面朝任何固定的罗盘方位。

branches.en: Inner placement: find your place in a new situation as if it had directions.
branches.cn: 内在定位：把新处境当作有方向的空间，在其中找到自己的位置。

branches.en: Purpose and poetry: turn toward a goal, or keep the old sense of the rising sun.
branches.cn: 目的与诗意：转向一个目标，或保留“正在升起的太阳”的古义。

intro.en: The ori- family is built on rising: sunrise, beginning, and being born all share one Latin verb.
intro.cn: ori- 词族围绕“升起”构建：日出、开端、出生都共用一个拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin oriri 'to rise' gives oriens 'rising, east', orientalis 'eastern', and origo 'beginning, source'. English orient, origin, and abort all descend from this verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oriri“升起”产生 oriens“升起的、东方”、orientalis“东方的”、origo“开端、来源”。英语的 orient、origin、abort 都出自这个动词。

items.meaning: the east; to place facing a reference point
items.meaningCN: 东方；使朝向某个参照点
items.example: The room was oriented to catch the morning sun.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间被布置成能接住晨光。

items.meaning: of or belonging to the east
items.example: The museum holds a large oriental collection.
items.exampleCN: 这家博物馆藏有大量东方文物。

items.meaning: the act of finding direction; the direction faced
items.example: New employees attend a two-day orientation.
items.exampleCN: 新员工参加为期两天的入职导览。

items.meaning: to make someone lose their bearings
items.example: The mirrored corridors disoriented the visitors.
items.exampleCN: 镜面走廊让参观者迷失了方向。

items.meaning: the state of losing one's sense of direction
items.example: Jet lag can cause temporary disorientation.
items.exampleCN: 时差反应会造成暂时的方向感混乱。

items.meaning: to give a new direction to something
items.example: The company reoriented its strategy toward Asia.
items.exampleCN: 公司把战略重新调整为面向亚洲。

items.meaning: a sport of finding one's way across country with map and compass
items.example: Orienteering rewards careful map reading.
items.exampleCN: 定向越野考验细致的读图能力。

items.meaning: the point where something begins or comes from
items.example: The origin of the custom is unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗的起源不明。

items.meaning: literally 'to fail to rise'; to stop before completion
items.meaningCN: 字面“未能升起”；中止、流产
items.example: The mission was aborted because of the storm.
items.exampleCN: 任务因暴风雨而中止。

latinEntries.meaning: to rise, get up, appear above the horizon, be born
latinEntries.meaningCN: 升起、起身、出现在地平线上、出生
latinEntries.example: Sol oritur means the sun rises.
latinEntries.exampleCN: Sol oritur 意为太阳升起。

latinEntries.meaning: rising; the east; the rising sun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 升起的；东方；升起的太阳
latinEntries.example: Oriens is the source of French orient.
latinEntries.exampleCN: oriens 是法语 orient 的来源。

latinEntries.meaning: of or belonging to the east
latinEntries.example: Orientalis is the source of English oriental.
latinEntries.exampleCN: orientalis 是英语 oriental 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Origo is the source of English origin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: origo 是英语 origin 的来源。

definition_zh: 结果；结局；成果；结局指标
definition_en: the result or final situation produced by an event, process, decision, or treatment
core_image: 一条路走到尽头，终点处落下一个清晰的印记
scene: 临床试验结束时，研究团队把两组康复率并排写进同一张表。The main outcome was clear: the treated group recovered twelve points more often than the control group.
sceneCN: 这里 outcome 是“（研究或临床的）结局指标”（第 8 个义项：统计意义上的终点指标）；句意：主要结局指标很清楚：用药组的康复率比对照组高出十二个百分点。图中可辨识物件：病历表、统计柱状图、药瓶、研究记录。

derivatives.zh: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的

senses.title: The result of an event or process
senses.definition: the result or final situation that follows from an event or process
senses.definitionCN: 由某个事件或过程产生的最终结果或局面
senses.example: The outcome of the experiment surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 实验的结果让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: The word is a compound of out and come: something comes out of a process and stands at the end of it. The result is pictured as a thing that emerges and becomes visible once the process is finished.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 out 与 come 复合而成：某物从过程里“走出来”，停在过程的末端。结果被想象成一件在过程结束后浮现、变得可见的东西。

senses.title: A consequence of a decision
senses.definition: the effect that a decision or action has, often considered before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 某个决定或行动带来的效果，常在做出决定前就被考虑
senses.example: Before you speak, consider the outcome of your words.
senses.exampleCN: 开口之前，先想想你的话会带来什么后果。
senses.why: The same emergence is now read backwards as consequence: the decision sends something out, and that something returns as the situation you must live in.
senses.whyCN: 同样的“浮现”现在被反向读成后果：决定送出某样东西，而那样东西又作为你必须生活在其中的局面返回。

senses.title: The result of a contest or vote
senses.definition: the final result of an election, trial, game, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 选举、审判、比赛或谈判的最终结果
senses.example: The outcome of the election remained unclear for days.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果数日未明。
senses.why: A contest is a process with a single end point, so outcome fits it naturally. The word does not say who won; it names the shape the whole process leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 竞赛是一个有单一终点的过程，因此 outcome 天然适用。这个词不说明谁赢，只命名整个过程留下的那个形状。

senses.title: A medical or clinical result
senses.definition: the health result of a treatment or illness for a patient or group
senses.definitionCN: 治疗或疾病给患者或群体带来的健康结果
senses.example: Better hygiene led to improved patient outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的卫生条件改善了患者的治疗结果。
senses.why: Medicine turns the everyday word into a measured endpoint: the process is treatment, and what comes out at the end is the patient's condition. The metaphor of emergence becomes a chart.
senses.whyCN: 医学把日常词变成可测量的终点：过程是治疗，末端“走出来”的是患者的状况。浮现的比喻变成了一张图表。

senses.title: The expected or desired result
senses.definition: the result that people hope for or predict, often stated in advance
senses.definitionCN: 人们希望或预测的结果，常被提前说明
senses.example: The negotiators aimed for a fair outcome for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者力求让双方都得到公平的结果。
senses.why: Once the end point is known to be a result, it can be wished for before it exists. The word stops describing what happened and starts naming a target placed at the end of the process.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道末端是一个结果，它就可以在存在之前被期盼。这个词于是不再描述已发生的事，而是命名一个被放在过程末端的目标。

senses.title: A learning outcome in education
senses.definition: a specific skill or understanding that students are expected to gain from a course
senses.definitionCN: 学生预期从课程中获得的具体技能或理解
senses.example: Each lesson lists three learning outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 每节课都列出三项学习成果。
senses.why: Education reverses the direction: instead of asking what came out of teaching, it first declares what should come out. The outcome becomes a designed destination rather than a report.
senses.whyCN: 教育把方向倒过来：不是问教学之后“出来了什么”，而是先声明“应该出来什么”。结果由事后报告变成事先设计的目的地。

senses.title: The result of a legal case
senses.definition: the final decision or settlement of a legal dispute or court case
senses.definitionCN: 法律争议或法庭案件的最终裁决或和解
senses.example: The case outcome depended on one witness.
senses.exampleCN: 案件结果取决于一名证人。
senses.why: A trial is a bounded procedure with an official end, so its result is called an outcome rather than a mere effect. The word suits any process that is formally closed.
senses.whyCN: 审判是一个有官方终点的有限程序，因此它的结果被称为 outcome，而不只是 effect。这个词适用于任何正式结束的过程。

senses.title: A measured endpoint in research
senses.definition: a variable that researchers measure at the end of a study to judge whether an intervention worked
senses.definitionCN: 研究者在研究结束时测量、用来判断干预是否有效的变量
senses.example: Recovery rate was the primary outcome of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 康复率是该试验的主要终点指标。
senses.why: Statistics narrows outcome to one measured thing among many possible results. The end of the process is now a designated variable, chosen before the data are collected so the question cannot be moved afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把 outcome 收窄为众多可能结果中被选定测量的一项。过程的末端现在是一个事先指定的变量，在收集数据前就定好，以免事后移动问题。

intro.en: Outcome is not Latin at all. It is a Scottish English compound of two native words, and its history shows the modern sense is surprisingly late.
intro.cn: outcome 根本不是拉丁词。它是两个英语本族词构成的苏格兰英语复合词，其历史显示现代义出现得相当晚。

items.en: c. 1200, out-coming was used for 'an emergence, act or fact of coming out'. Old English had utancumen 'stranger, foreigner', literally 'one who came from outside'.
items.cn: 约 1200 年，out-coming 表示“出现、出来的行为或事实”。古英语有 utancumen“陌生人、外来者”，字面是“从外面来的人”。

items.en: The noun outcome is recorded in 1788, originally Scottish, meaning 'that which results from something'. It comes from the verbal phrase out + come.
items.cn: 名词 outcome 记录于 1788 年，最初见于苏格兰，义为“由某事物产生的结果”。它来自动词短语 out + come。

items.en: Popularized in English by Thomas Carlyle around the 1830s, according to standard references.
items.cn: 据通行资料，托马斯·卡莱尔在 1830 年代前后使这个词在英语中流行开来。

items.en: The word stays a transparent compound: out (forth, into view) + come (arrive). Its force is that the result is something that came out and can now be seen.
items.cn: 这个词始终是透明的复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（到达）。它的力量在于：结果是“走出来”、现在能被看见的东西。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine, education, and statistics turned outcome into a countable endpoint: patient outcome, learning outcome, primary outcome.
items.cn: 20 世纪的医学、教育与统计学把 outcome 变成可计数的终点：patient outcome、learning outcome、primary outcome。

note.en: The first group separates other out- compounds; the second ranks the main synonyms by where they place the result.
note.cn: 第一组把其他 out- 复合词分开；第二组按“结果被放在哪里”来区分主要近义词。

entries.definition: the amount produced by a machine, worker, or system. It is what is put out, not the situation that results.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、工人或系统的产出量。它是“被放出来的量”，不是最终形成的局面。

entries.definition: the result that comes out of a process and remains as its end state.
entries.definitionCN: 从过程中出来、并作为其终态留存下来的结果。

entries.definition: the sudden start of disease, war, or violence. It names a breaking out, not a result.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病、战争或暴力的突然爆发。它指“破壳而出”，不是结果。

entries.definition: a view or forecast. It is what you look out at, or forward to, not what came out.
entries.definitionCN: 景色；前景展望。它是你向外看、向前看的东西，不是出来的结果。

entries.definition: what happens because of something else. It is the broadest term and can name anything from a sum to a consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 因另一事物而发生的事。它是最宽泛的词，可以指从计算结果到后果的任何东西。

entries.definition: a result that follows logically or causally, often with a sense of importance or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 按逻辑或因果随之而来的结果，常含重要性或责任意味。

entries.definition: the change produced by a cause. It stresses the change itself rather than the final situation.
entries.definitionCN: 原因造成的变化。它强调变化本身，而不是最终局面。

entries.definition: the final or eventual result of a series of events. It is informal and stresses the end of a long story.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列事件最终的结局。它较口语化，强调一个长故事的最后收束。

normalIntro.en: Five spelling hooks, then three abstract pictures of a process arriving at its end.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个拼写钩子，再用三个“过程抵达终点”的抽象画面。

normal.en: out + come: what comes out at the end.
normal.cn: out + come：最后“走出来”的那个东西。

normal.en: outcome ends in -come just as become: something becomes visible at the end.
normal.cn: outcome 和 become 一样以 -come 结尾：某物在最后变得可见。

normal.en: An election outcome is the scoreboard after the last vote is counted.
normal.cn: 选举的 outcome 就是最后一张票计完后那块记分牌。

normal.en: Learning outcomes are written before the course, like a destination on a ticket.
normal.cn: learning outcomes 写在课程之前，像车票上的目的地。

normal.en: Primary outcome is the one number a trial promises to report.
normal.cn: primary outcome 是一项试验承诺要报告的那个数字。

abstract.en: An outcome is the shape a process leaves behind after it stops moving.
abstract.cn: 结果是过程停止运动后留下的那个形状。

abstract.en: You can design an outcome without being able to control it: the end is a target, not a guarantee.
abstract.cn: 你可以设计一个结果，却无法控制它：终点是目标，不是保证。

abstract.en: Every decision sends something out into the world, and that something comes back as the room you live in.
abstract.cn: 每个决定都往世界里送出某样东西，而那样东西会作为你居住的房间返回。

examples.en: No one could predict the outcome of the talks.
examples.cn: 没有人能预测会谈的结果。

examples.en: The study measured three outcomes: pain, mobility, and sleep quality.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了三个结局指标：疼痛、活动能力与睡眠质量。

examples.en: A good process does not always produce a good outcome.
examples.cn: 好的过程并不总能产生好的结果。

dict_mnemonic.note: 记成“从过程里走出来（out）并到达（come）的东西”。
dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ come（来）→ 出来的结果 → 结果、结局

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外、进入视野）+ come（来）；1788 年见于苏格兰英语，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from any result, to consequences and contest results, then to measured endpoints in medicine, education, law, and statistics.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从任何“结果”出发，走到后果与比赛结果，再到医学、教育、法律与统计中可测量的终点。

core.en: A path reaching its end, where a mark is left behind
core.cn: 一条路走到尽头，在那里留下一个印记

branches.en: General result: what an event or process finally produced.
branches.cn: 一般结果：一个事件或过程最终产生的东西。

branches.en: Formal endings: the result of a contest, or of a legal case.
branches.cn: 正式终点：比赛的结果，或案件的结果。

branches.en: Measured endings: a patient's health result, or a study's primary endpoint.
branches.cn: 可测量的终点：患者的健康结果，或研究的主要终点。

branches.en: Ends declared in advance: a hoped-for result, or a learning outcome.
branches.cn: 事先声明的终点：期望的结果，或学习成果。

branches.en: Consequence: the word looks back at what a decision cost.
branches.cn: 后果：这个词回看一个决定付出了什么代价。

intro.en: Outcome belongs to the huge out- family and the even larger come family. Both halves are native English, so there is no Latin root here.
intro.cn: outcome 属于庞大的 out- 词族，也属于更大的 come 词族。两半都是英语本族词，因此这里没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: out is Old English ut, from Proto-Germanic *ut-, and come is Old English cuman, from Proto-Germanic *kwem-.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：out 是古英语 ut，来自原始日耳曼语 *ut-；come 是古英语 cuman，来自原始日耳曼语 *kwem-。

items.meaning: that which comes out of a process
items.example: The outcome was better than expected.
items.exampleCN: 结果比预期更好。

items.meaning: an emergence; a result (now rare)
items.example: The outcoming of the vote was delayed.
items.exampleCN: 投票结果的公布被推迟了。

items.meaning: to move toward and arrive at a point
items.example: Spring comes early here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的春天来得早。

items.meaning: money that comes in
items.example: Her income doubled after the promotion.
items.exampleCN: 升职后她的收入翻了一倍。

items.meaning: to get over an obstacle and win through
items.example: They overcame the shortage of funds.
items.exampleCN: 他们克服了资金短缺。

items.meaning: about to come; willing to give information
items.meaningCN: 即将到来的；乐于提供信息的
items.example: The forthcoming report will cover the trial.
items.exampleCN: 即将发布的报告将涵盖这项试验。

items.meaning: an arrival; the approach of something
items.example: The coming of winter changed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 冬天的到来改变了计划。

items.meaning: to come to be; to grow into
items.example: The sky became dark.
items.exampleCN: 天色变暗了。

items.meaning: a variable used to judge a result in research
items.example: Pain score was the main outcome measure.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛评分是主要的结局测量指标。

definition_zh: 产量；产出；输出；输出数据；生产
definition_en: the amount produced by a person, machine, or system; data or energy sent out; to produce or send out
core_image: 工厂传送带末端，成品一件件被放到外面
scene: 工厂升级设备后，工程师站在传送带旁盯着成品箱。Hourly output rose from 120 units to 180 units in the first week.
sceneCN: 这里 output 是“单位时间内的产量”（第 1 个义项：生产出来的数量）；句意：每小时的产量在第一周就从 120 件提高到 180 件。图中可辨识物件：传送带、成品箱、白板、秒表。

derivatives.zh: 输出设备；输出者（技术语境）

senses.title: The quantity produced
senses.definition: the amount of goods or work produced in a given time
senses.definitionCN: 在给定时间内生产出的货物或工作量
senses.example: The factory doubled its output in three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在三年内把产量翻了一倍。
senses.why: Output began in 1839 as a technical term of the iron and coal trades: the material put out of the works. The word does not name the goods themselves but the quantity that comes out of the process.
senses.whyCN: output 在 1839 年作为钢铁与煤炭行业的技术词出现：被“放到外面”的材料。它命名的不是货物本身，而是从过程中出来的数量。

senses.title: Energy delivered by a device
senses.definition: the power, energy, or signal that a machine or system delivers
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统输送出的功率、能量或信号
senses.example: The solar array has an output of five kilowatts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个太阳能阵列的输出功率为五千瓦。
senses.why: By 1884 output named 'energy produced by a device or system'. The industrial image is kept, but what comes out is now electricity or a signal rather than coal.
senses.whyCN: 到 1884 年，output 指“设备或系统产生的能量”。工业画面保留下来，只是出来的东西变成了电或信号，而不是煤。

senses.title: Data produced by a computer
senses.definition: the data, results, or display that a computer sends to a user or another device
senses.definitionCN: 计算机发送给用户或其他设备的数据、结果或显示内容
senses.example: Check the output for error messages.
senses.exampleCN: 检查输出里有没有错误信息。
senses.why: Computing adopts the same schema: a program takes input in and puts output out. The metaphor of a factory becomes a flow of characters on a terminal.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用同一图式：程序把输入拿进来，把输出放出去。工厂的比喻变成了终端上流动的字符。

senses.title: Work produced by a researcher or artist
senses.titleCN: 研究者或创作者的产出
senses.definition: the amount or quality of work that a person, team, or field produces
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或领域所生产工作的数量或质量
senses.example: Her research output rose after she left teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 离开教学岗位后，她的研究产出增加了。
senses.why: The word extends from things to work: papers, books, and paintings are also what comes out of a process. Output measures volume, while quality is a separate question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从实物延伸到作品：论文、书、画也是过程里出来的东西。output 衡量的是数量，质量则是另一个问题。

senses.title: To produce or emit something
senses.definition: to produce, generate, or send out goods, data, energy, or sound
senses.definitionCN: 生产、产生或发出货物、数据、能量或声音
senses.example: The speakers output a low hum.
senses.exampleCN: 扬声器发出低低的嗡鸣。
senses.why: The verb 'to produce' appears in 1858, long after the noun. What was a thing at the end of a process becomes an action: the system outputs whatever it sends forth.
senses.whyCN: 动词“生产”义出现于 1858 年，比名词晚得多。原本位于过程末端的“东西”变成了动作：系统输出它所送出的任何内容。

senses.title: Obsolete: to expel or exclude
senses.definition: in older use, to expel or shut something out
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，表示逐出或排除某物
senses.example: The older verb meant to put a person out of a place.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的动词义是“把人赶出一个地方”。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from the mid-14c. in the sense 'expel, exclude', which is now obsolete. The literal 'put out' is the seed from which both 'produce' and 'exclude' grew in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 该动词在 14 世纪中期记录的义项是“逐出、排除”，现已废弃。字面的“放到外面”是一颗种子，向两个方向长出了“生产”和“排除”。

senses.title: Creative or athletic yield
senses.definition: the total amount of creative work or performance produced over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内产生的创作或表演总量
senses.example: The band's output slowed during the tour.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演期间乐队的产出放缓了。
senses.why: Output treats creative work as measurable production. The image is quantitative: a career can be counted like a factory shift, even if the value of each piece cannot.
senses.whyCN: output 把创作当成可测量的生产。这个画面是数量化的：一段职业生涯可以像工厂班次一样被计数，尽管每件作品的价值无法这样计算。

senses.title: A signal or terminal that sends data
senses.titleCN: 发送数据的信号或端口
senses.definition: an output terminal, port, or channel through which a device sends signals
senses.definitionCN: 设备借以发送信号的输出端、端口或通道
senses.example: Connect the monitor to the video output.
senses.exampleCN: 把显示器接到视频输出端口。
senses.why: Here output names not the data but the doorway it leaves through. The noun shifts from what comes out to the place of exit, a common pattern in technical vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 这里 output 指的不是数据，而是数据离开的那扇门。名词从“出来的东西”转到“出口的位置”，这是技术词汇里常见的转义方式。

intro.en: Output is a native English compound, first a technical trade term and then a general word for production. No Latin root is involved.
intro.cn: output 是英语本族复合词，先是行业技术词，后成为一般的“产出”词。不涉及拉丁词根。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the mid-14c. meaning 'to expel, exclude', a literal 'put out'. This sense is now obsolete.
items.cn: 动词记录于 14 世纪中期，义为“逐出、排除”，即字面的“放到外面”。这一义项现已废弃。

items.en: The noun appears meaning 'quantity of material put out or produced in a given time'. Until about 1880 it was a technical term in the iron and coal trade.
items.cn: 名词出现，义为“在给定时间内产出或生产的材料数量”。直到约 1880 年，它都是钢铁与煤炭行业的技术词。

items.en: The verb gains the modern sense 'to produce', while the 1884 noun sense 'energy produced by a device or system' follows.
items.cn: 动词获得现代义“生产”；随后 1884 年名词出现“设备或系统产生的能量”这一义项。

items.en: Computing makes output half of the input/output pair. Research and economics extend it to papers, data, and national production.
items.cn: 计算机领域让 output 成为 input/output 这对概念的一半。科研与经济学把它扩展到论文、数据与国家生产。

items.en: The compound stays transparent: out (forth) + put (place, thrust). Something is placed outward, and that outward placement is the output.
items.cn: 这个复合词始终透明：out（向外）+ put（放置、推）。某物被放到外面，而这次“向外放置”就是 output。

note.en: The look-alike group separates out- compounds; the near-meaning group separates quantity from result and from input.
note.cn: 形近组区分其他 out- 复合词；近义组区分“数量”“结果”与“投入”。

entries.definition: the result that comes out of a process. It is the end state, not the quantity produced.
entries.definitionCN: 过程产生的结果。它是终态，不是生产数量。

entries.definition: what is put into a system: materials, data, or effort. It is the mirror image of output.
entries.definitionCN: 投入系统的材料、数据或人力。它是 output 的镜像。

entries.definition: a small military or trading settlement far from the main base. It is a place put out, not a quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 远离主基地的军事或贸易据点。它是被放到外面的地点，不是数量。

entries.definition: the beginning of something. It marks the start, the opposite end from output's product.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的开端。它标记起点，与 output 的产物处在相反的一端。

entries.definition: the act or process of making goods. It names the activity; output names the amount that results.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的行为或过程。它命名活动；output 命名由此产生的数量。

entries.definition: the amount produced, especially by land or an investment. It often implies a return on effort or capital.
entries.definitionCN: 产量，尤指土地或投资带来的收益。它常含“投入的回报”之意。

entries.definition: output measured per unit of input, such as per hour or per worker. It is a ratio, not a total.
entries.definitionCN: 每单位投入（如每小时或每人）所对应的产出。它是比率，不是总量。

entries.definition: what follows from an action or process. It can be abstract; output is usually measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 由行动或过程产生的东西。它可以是抽象的；output 通常可测量。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on 'put out', then three abstract images.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个围绕“放到外面”的钩子，再用三个抽象画面。

normal.en: output = put out: whatever the system places outside itself.
normal.cn: output＝put out：系统放到自己外面的东西。

normal.en: input goes in, output comes out: the same put, opposite doors.
normal.cn: input 进，output 出：同一个 put，方向相反的两扇门。

normal.en: A factory's output is counted in units per hour, like a heartbeat monitor.
normal.cn: 工厂的 output 按每小时多少件来计数，像心跳监护仪上的数字。

normal.en: Computer output is what appears on the screen after the program has put it out.
normal.cn: 计算机的 output 就是程序“放到外面”后出现在屏幕上的内容。

normal.en: Audio output is the sound that leaves the speaker.
normal.cn: audio output 是离开扬声器的声音。

abstract.en: Output measures how much a system gives to the world, not how much it is worth.
abstract.cn: output 衡量一个系统给了世界多少，而不是它值多少。

abstract.en: Every system has a door: what goes in is input, what leaves is output.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都有一扇门：进去的是 input，离开的是 output。

abstract.en: A person can be counted like a factory and still be unmeasurable as a mind.
abstract.cn: 一个人可以像工厂一样被计数，却仍然无法作为一个心灵被测量。

examples.en: The mine's output fell after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，这座矿的产量下降了。

examples.en: Please save the program's output to a text file.
examples.cn: 请把程序的输出保存到一个文本文件。

examples.en: The new turbine outputs twice as much power as the old one.
examples.cn: 新涡轮机的输出功率是旧机的两倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ put（放）→ 放到外面的东西 → 产出、输出

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外）+ put（放置）；1839 年见于钢铁与煤炭行业，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from industrial quantity, to energy, computer data, creative work, and finally the act of emitting or the port that emits.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从工业产量，走到能量、计算机数据、创作成果，最后落到“发出”的动作或发出数据的端口。

core.en: Finished goods placed outside the factory gate
core.cn: 成品被放到工厂大门之外

branches.en: Measured production: goods per hour, or power delivered by a device.
branches.cn: 可测量的生产：每小时多少件，或设备输送的功率。

branches.en: Computer output and the port it leaves through.
branches.cn: 计算机输出，以及它离开时经过的端口。

branches.en: Human production: research papers, books, songs, performances.
branches.cn: 人的产出：论文、书、歌曲、表演。

branches.en: The verb: a system outputs whatever it sends forth.
branches.cn: 动词义：系统输出它所送出的任何东西。

branches.en: The obsolete literal sense: to put someone out, to expel.
branches.cn: 已废弃的字面义：把人放到外面，即逐出。

intro.en: Output sits in a productive family of compounds built with out- and put. The same two elements also make input and throughput.
intro.cn: output 处在由 out- 与 put 构成的活跃复合词族中。同样两个元素还造出了 input 与 throughput。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: put is of uncertain Germanic origin, recorded in late Old English as *putian 'to thrust, push'.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：put 的日耳曼来源不确定，古英语晚期记为 *putian“推、刺”。

items.meaning: what is placed out; the amount produced
items.meaningCN: 被放到外面的东西；产量
items.example: Output rose by ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 产量上升了百分之十。

items.meaning: what is put in: materials, data, or effort
items.example: Better input usually improves output.
items.exampleCN: 更好的投入通常会改善产出。

items.meaning: the amount a system can process in a period
items.example: The server's throughput is limited by memory.
items.exampleCN: 服务器的吞吐量受内存限制。

items.meaning: to place, thrust, or set something somewhere
items.meaningCN: 放置、推、把某物放到某处
items.example: Put the box by the door.
items.exampleCN: 把箱子放在门边。

items.meaning: a device or routine that outputs data
items.meaningCN: 输出设备；执行输出的程序
items.example: The printer is a slow outputter.
items.exampleCN: 这台打印机是慢速输出设备。

items.meaning: an outer or outlying port
items.example: Goods were shipped through the outport.
items.exampleCN: 货物经由外港运出。

items.meaning: leaving; friendly and sociable
items.example: Outgoing mail is collected at noon.
items.exampleCN: 寄出的邮件中午收取。

items.meaning: money spent, literally laid out
items.example: The initial outlay was high.
items.exampleCN: 初期支出很高。

items.meaning: a place or channel through which something leaves
items.example: The river has only one outlet.
items.exampleCN: 这条河只有一个出口。

definition_zh: 全面的；总体的；总共；总体来说；（overalls）工装裤
definition_en: including everything; considered as a whole; in general; (overalls) a protective garment worn over other clothes
core_image: 从高处俯视整张地图，所有街道一次收进眼里
scene: 项目复盘会上，负责人先讲细节，再把进度曲线和预算表并排贴好。Her overall judgment was simple: the project was a little late, but the quality and the budget were still under control.
sceneCN: 这里 overall 是“总体的、把一切算在内的”（第 1 个义项：包括全部）；句意：她的总体判断很简单：项目略慢，但质量与预算都在可控范围内。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、进度曲线、预算表、会议桌。

collocations.zh: 总体来说，这个计划可行

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Including everything
senses.definition: covering or including all parts, without leaving anything out
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖或包括所有部分，不遗漏任何一项
senses.example: The overall cost of the project was higher than planned.
senses.exampleCN: 项目的总成本高于计划。
senses.why: Overall began as over + all, 'everywhere, in every part'. The modern 1894 sense 'taking all into consideration' keeps the same picture: the word spreads over the whole instead of standing inside one part.
senses.whyCN: overall 原为 over + all，意为“到处、在每个部分”。1894 年的现代义“把一切考虑在内”保留同一画面：这个词铺在整个整体之上，而不是站在某一部分里。

senses.title: The total amount
senses.definition: the combined amount after all parts have been added together
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分相加后的合计量
senses.example: Overall spending rose by six percent.
senses.exampleCN: 总支出上升了百分之六。
senses.why: Once the word covers all parts, it can name their sum. The movement is from spatial coverage to arithmetic total: everything is gathered under one figure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词覆盖所有部分，它就能命名它们的总和。意义从空间覆盖转到算术合计：一切被收拢到一个数字之下。

senses.title: A general impression
senses.definition: a judgment based on the whole rather than on separate details
senses.definitionCN: 基于整体而非各个细节作出的判断
senses.example: My overall impression was of a well-run school.
senses.exampleCN: 我的总体印象是这是一所管理良好的学校。
senses.why: An impression formed 'over all' is built by stepping back from details. The word marks the level at which separate observations merge into one feeling.
senses.whyCN: “覆盖全部”形成的印象，是从细节退后一步得到的。这个词标记的是各个观察合并成一种感受的那个层级。

senses.title: The whole picture
senses.definition: the complete situation seen as one connected picture
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个相互关联的整体来看的完整局面
senses.example: The report gives an overall picture of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告给出了该地区的整体图景。
senses.why: The metaphor is visual: an observer moves above the parts and sees how they fit. Overall names that altitude of view, not the individual objects below.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是视觉性的：观察者升到各部分之上，看见它们如何拼合。overall 命名的是这个观察高度，而不是下方的单个物体。

senses.title: Generally speaking
senses.definition: used to sum up a judgment after weighing the details
senses.definitionCN: 在权衡细节之后用来概括判断
senses.example: Overall, the experiment succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 总体来说，实验是成功的。
senses.why: As an adverb, the word performs the summing-up act itself. It tells the listener that the sentence to follow is a verdict after the parts have been counted, not another detail.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时，这个词本身就在做“汇总”这个动作。它告诉听者：接下来的句子是清点完各部分后的裁决，而不是又一条细节。

senses.title: Overalls: a garment worn over all
senses.titleCN: 工装裤：穿在其他衣服外面的衣物
senses.definition: a protective garment, usually trousers with a bib, worn over ordinary clothes
senses.definitionCN: 穿在日常衣服外面的防护衣物，通常是有胸兜的裤子
senses.example: The mechanic wiped his hands on his overalls.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工在工装裤上擦了擦手。
senses.why: The noun overalls uses the literal spatial sense: a garment worn over all the other clothes. The same 'covering everything' idea that governs the adjective is here made of cloth.
senses.whyCN: 名词 overalls 用的是字面空间义：穿在所有其他衣服外面的衣物。支配形容词的“覆盖全部”观念，在这里是用布做成的。

senses.title: Combined-score champion
senses.definition: the winner judged on the total of all events rather than a single one
senses.definitionCN: 按所有项目的总和而非单项评出的优胜者
senses.example: She took the overall title by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 她以两分之差拿下总冠军。
senses.why: In sport, overall marks the level at which separate events are added into one standing. The word directs attention away from any single race and toward the whole series.
senses.whyCN: 在体育中，overall 标记的是把各单项加总成一个总排名的层级。这个词把注意力从任何一场比赛移开，转向整个系列赛。

senses.title: Whole-system responsibility
senses.definition: responsibility for the whole of an operation rather than one part of it
senses.definitionCN: 对整个运作而非某一部分负责
senses.example: He has overall responsibility for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 他对安全负总责。
senses.why: This use turns the spatial word into an organizational one: a person stands above all the parts and answers for how they work together. Coverage becomes accountability.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法把空间词变成组织词：一个人站在所有部分之上，对它们如何协同负责。覆盖变成了问责。

intro.en: Overall is native English, built from over and all. Its oldest sense was 'everywhere'; the modern 'all things considered' is only from 1894.
intro.cn: overall 是英语本族词，由 over 与 all 构成。最古老的义项是“到处”；现代“把所有事都考虑在内”的义项直到 1894 年才出现。

items.en: The phrase ofer eall meant 'everywhere, in every part or place'. The modern spelling overall comes from Middle English over-al.
items.cn: 短语 ofer eall 意为“到处、在每个部分或地方”。现代拼写 overall 来自中世纪英语 over-al。

items.en: Over-al kept the sense 'everywhere'. That original sense is now obsolete in standard English.
items.cn: over-al 保留“到处”之义。这个原始义项在现代标准英语中已废弃。

items.en: The modern meaning 'including everything, taking all into consideration' is recorded.
items.cn: 现代义“包括一切、把全部考虑在内”被记录。

items.en: The garment sense of overalls (trousers worn over other clothes) belongs to the same literal idea of something worn over all.
items.cn: overalls（穿在其他衣服外面的裤子）的衣物义，同属“穿在所有东西外面”这一字面观念。具体年代各家说法不一，此处只取通行理解。

items.en: The word now works as adjective, adverb, and noun. Its unity is the idea of a view or covering that spans every part.
items.cn: 这个词现在是形容词、副词和名词。它的统一性在于一个横跨每个部分的视角或覆盖。

note.en: The look-alike group separates other over- compounds; the near-meaning group ranks words by how much they include.
note.cn: 形近组区分其他 over- 复合词；近义组按“包含多少”来区分。

entries.definition: including everything, or considered as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 包括一切，或作为整体来考虑。

entries.definition: too much; excessively. It is over- with the negative sense 'too', not 'covering all'.
entries.definitionCN: 过度地；太。它用的是 over- 的负面义“太”，不是“覆盖全部”。

entries.definition: above one's head; also fixed business costs. The over- is spatial or figurative, not inclusive.
entries.definitionCN: 头顶上的；也指企业固定开销。这里的 over- 是空间或比喻义，不表示“包括”。

entries.definition: beyond the sea. The over- means 'across', not 'covering everything'.
entries.definitionCN: 海外的。over- 表示“越过”，不是“覆盖一切”。

entries.definition: complete in amount; the whole sum. It is quantitative, while overall can also mean a general judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 数量上完整的；总和。它偏数量，而 overall 也可指总体判断。

entries.definition: covering the main features rather than details. It stresses breadth of scope, not the act of summing up.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖主要特征而非细节。它强调范围的宽，而不是汇总的动作。

entries.definition: including nearly all relevant items. It is stronger and more formal than overall and usually implies a deliberate completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 包括几乎所有相关项目。它比 overall 更强、更正式，通常暗示刻意的完整。

entries.definition: considering everything; generally. It is the adverbial phrase closest to overall in its summing-up use.
entries.definitionCN: 总的来说；大体上。它是最接近 overall 汇总用法的副词短语。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on over + all, then three abstract images of a view from above.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个 over + all 的钩子，再用三个“从高处看”的抽象画面。

normal.en: over + all: the view that goes over every part.
normal.cn: over + all：越过每一个部分的视角。

normal.en: overall ends with all, so it always includes everything.
normal.cn: overall 以 all 结尾，所以它总是把一切包含进来。

normal.en: overalls are worn over all your other clothes: same word, made of cloth.
normal.cn: overalls 穿在你所有其他衣服外面：同一个词，只是用布做成了。

normal.en: Overall, the plan works: the comma marks the step back from details.
normal.cn: Overall, the plan works：这个逗号标记从细节退后一步。

normal.en: An overall winner is not the winner of one race but of the whole series.
normal.cn: overall winner 不是某一场比赛的赢家，而是整个系列赛的赢家。

abstract.en: To see overall is to change altitude: details do not disappear, they become pattern.
abstract.cn: 看“整体”就是换高度：细节没有消失，而是变成了图案。

abstract.en: Every whole is a decision about which parts to count and which to leave outside the frame.
abstract.cn: 每个“整体”都是一次决定：哪些部分算进来，哪些留在画框之外。

abstract.en: Overall judgment is what remains after the numbers stop arguing with each other.
abstract.cn: 总体判断，就是数字之间不再互相争吵之后剩下的东西。

examples.en: Overall, the trip was a success despite the delays.
examples.cn: 尽管有延误，总体来说这次旅行是成功的。

examples.en: The overall budget includes travel, staff, and equipment.
examples.cn: 总预算包括差旅、人员与设备。

examples.en: He wore overalls and a heavy shirt in the workshop.
examples.cn: 他在车间里穿着工装裤和厚衬衫。

dict_mnemonic.note: 记成“从所有（all）之上（over）看下去”。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（在上、越过）+ all（全部）→ 覆盖全部的 → 总体的、总体来说

root: 英语本族复合词：over（在上、越过）+ all（全部），古英语 ofer eall“到处”；无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from spatial coverage, to totals, impressions, the whole picture, the summing-up adverb, the garment, combined titles, and whole-system responsibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从空间覆盖，走到总量、印象、整体图景、汇总副词、衣物、综合头衔与整体责任。

core.en: A view from above that gathers every part into one frame
core.cn: 从高处把每个部分收进一个画框的视角

branches.en: Coverage and sum: all parts included, then all parts added.
branches.cn: 覆盖与合计：先包括所有部分，再把所有部分相加。

branches.en: Perception: an impression or picture formed by stepping back.
branches.cn: 感知：退后一步形成的印象或图景。

branches.en: The adverb as a verdict: the sentence that follows is a summary.
branches.cn: 副词作裁决：接下来的句子是一个总结。

branches.en: Clothing: the literal covering worn over all other clothes.
branches.cn: 衣物：字面意义上穿在所有其他衣服外面的覆盖物。

branches.en: Institutions: a combined title, or accountability for the whole.
branches.cn: 制度层面：综合头衔，或对整个体系负责。

intro.en: Overall is a transparent compound of two very old native words. The over- prefix is shared with a large family; the all half is equally productive.
intro.cn: overall 是两个非常古老的英语本族词构成的透明复合词。over- 前缀与一个庞大词族共享，all 这一半也同样能产。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer (PIE *uper), and all is Old English eall, of uncertain connections outside Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer（原始印欧语 *uper），all 是古英语 eall，其在日耳曼语之外的关联不确定。

items.meaning: covering everything; considered as a whole
items.meaningCN: 覆盖一切；作为整体来考虑
items.example: Overall, sales were strong.
items.exampleCN: 总体而言，销售强劲。

items.meaning: a garment worn over other clothes
items.meaningCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的工装
items.example: The painter put on his overalls.
items.exampleCN: 油漆工穿上了工装裤。

items.meaning: above, across, more than
items.example: The plane flew over the city.
items.exampleCN: 飞机飞过城市上空。

items.meaning: the whole quantity; every part
items.example: All the seats were taken.
items.exampleCN: 所有座位都被占了。

items.meaning: excessively
items.example: The design is overly complex.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计过于复杂。

items.meaning: above the head; fixed costs
items.example: Overhead costs rose sharply.
items.exampleCN: 固定开销大幅上升。

items.meaning: a majority of all votes cast, not just of one group
items.meaningCN: 全部票数中的绝对多数
items.example: The party won an overall majority.
items.exampleCN: 该党赢得了绝对多数。

items.meaning: completely; in total
items.example: Altogether, ten people came.
items.exampleCN: 总共有十个人来了。

items.meaning: covering or affecting everything
items.example: The project has one overarching goal.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目有一个总揽全局的目标。

definition_zh: 重叠；部分覆盖同一区域；时间上部分重合；范围或职责部分相同；重叠部分；重叠量
definition_en: to cover part of the same surface, period, or range as something else, or to share part of it; also the shared part itself and its extent
core_image: 两张半透明胶片错开叠放，中间交叠的那一带颜色明显变深
scene: 调度员把白班和夜班的排班表铺在桌上。The two shifts overlap for one hour between seven and eight, and that hour is marked in dark ink.
sceneCN: 这里 overlap 是「时间上部分重合」（第 2 个义项：共用一段时间）；句意：两个班次在七点到八点之间重叠一小时，那一小时被涂成深色。图中可辨识物件：两张排班表、荧光笔、深色的一小时格子、值班帽。

pos.zh: 部分覆盖同一区域；交叠
（时间）部分重合；与……同时发生一段
（范围、兴趣、职责）部分相同；有交集

derivatives.zh: 已交叠的；被覆盖住一部分的

senses.title: Cover the same surface
senses.definition: to cover part of the same area of a surface as another thing
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物覆盖同一块表面的一部分
senses.example: The two labels overlap slightly at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 两张标签在角上略微重叠。
senses.why: Over- here means across or above, and lap means to fold or lay one thing over another. A layer laid across the edge of another shares a strip of surface with it, and that strip is the overlap.
senses.whyCN: over- 在这里是“越过、在上”，lap 是“折叠、把一层搭到另一层上”。一层越过另一层的边缘搭上去，两者就共用一条表面，这条共用的带子就是重叠。

senses.title: Share part of the same period
senses.definition: to happen during part of the same period as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事发生在同一段时间的一部分
senses.example: My lecture overlaps with the lab session on Thursday.
senses.exampleCN: 周四我的讲座和实验课时间重叠。
senses.why: When layers become schedules, the shared strip becomes shared minutes. The geometry is unchanged: two stretches laid along one line share a middle segment.
senses.whyCN: 当“层”变成“日程”，共用的那条带子就变成了共用的分钟。几何关系没有变：两条线段铺在同一条时间线上，中间有一段是双方都占着的。

senses.title: Share part of a range
senses.definition: to share part of a range of values, topics, or interests
senses.definitionCN: 在一段数值、话题或兴趣范围中有一部分相同
senses.example: Their research interests overlap in cognitive science.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的研究兴趣在认知科学上重叠。
senses.why: A range is a line with limits. Two ranges that share a stretch of that line overlap exactly as two strips share a band of surface, which is why the same word serves for both.
senses.whyCN: 范围是一条有端点的时间轴或数轴。两段范围共用其中一截，就像两条带子共用一段表面一样，因此同一个词可以同时用于空间、时间和抽象范围。

senses.title: Share duties: jobs that claim the same tasks
senses.titleCN: 职责重叠：两个岗位claim同一批任务
senses.definition: of jobs or responsibilities, to include the same tasks or territory
senses.definitionCN: 指岗位或职责包含同一批任务、同一片权责范围
senses.example: The two roles overlap, so one person could cover both.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个岗位职责重叠，一个人就能兼顾。
senses.why: Duties are territories drawn around tasks. When two job descriptions claim the same task, their territories share a zone; managers then redraw the boundaries to remove the overlap.
senses.whyCN: 职责是围绕任务划出的地盘。两份岗位说明都声称管同一件事时，它们的地盘就出现共用区；管理者随后要重划边界，消掉这块重叠。

senses.title: The shared part itself
senses.definition: the area, period, or set of items that two things both include
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物同时包含的区域、时段或项目集合
senses.example: The overlap between the two plans is small.
senses.exampleCN: 两个计划之间重叠的部分很小。
senses.why: English often turns the place where two things meet into a noun. The verb describes the laying across; the noun names the strip that results, as if you could point at it on a map.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把“两物相接之处”直接名词化。动词描述“搭过去”的动作，名词则指动作留下的那条带子，仿佛能在地图上指出来。

senses.title: How much is shared: measured overlap
senses.titleCN: 重叠量：被度量的重合程度
senses.definition: the extent to which two things cover the same ground, often given as a proportion
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物覆盖同一范围的程度，常以比例表示
senses.example: There is a 30 percent overlap between the two datasets.
senses.exampleCN: 两个数据集有百分之三十的重叠。
senses.why: Once the shared zone can be pointed at, it can be measured. Statistics and design turn the strip into a number, so overlap becomes a degree rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 共用区一旦能被指出来，就能被测量。统计学与设计把这条带子变成一个数字，于是重叠从“一个地方”变成了“一个程度”。

senses.title: Printing and imaging: lay one layer over another
senses.titleCN: 印刷与影像：一层压在一层上
senses.definition: in printing and image editing, to place or print one layer partly over another
senses.definitionCN: 在印刷与图像编辑中，把一层部分地压在另一层上
senses.example: The poster overlaps the photo with a red block.
senses.exampleCN: 海报用一个红色色块压住了照片的一部分。
senses.why: This is the craft sense at its most literal: ink or film laid across the edge of another layer. Where the two layers meet, the colours combine and the shared band darkens, which is exactly the image behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最字面的手艺义：油墨或胶片越过另一层的边缘压上去。两层相接处颜色叠加、共用带变深，正是这个词背后的原始画面。

senses.title: Handover overlap: both present for a while
senses.titleCN: 交接重叠期：两任同时在岗
senses.definition: a period when the outgoing and incoming person are both at work so that knowledge can pass between them
senses.definitionCN: 离任者与接任者同时在岗的一段时间，以便经验传递
senses.example: The new manager had a two-week overlap with her predecessor.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理与前任有两周的重叠期。
senses.why: In time, the shared strip can be deliberately arranged. It is the only window in which tacit knowledge can be shown rather than written down, so organizations schedule an overlap instead of a clean cut.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上，这条共用带子可以被刻意安排出来。它是默会知识能够“演示”而不是“写成文件”的唯一窗口，所以组织会安排一段重叠，而不是一刀切地换人。

intro.en: Overlap is a native English compound of two old words. The dates are recorded first uses, and the deeper origin of lap is not certain.
intro.cn: overlap 是两个古老英语本族词构成的复合词。年代为首次记录时间；lap 的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: The phrase lap over is recorded meaning 'to lie partly on or over something'. The image is a cloth or board laid across the edge of another.
items.cn: 短语 lap over 记录于 17 世纪 30 年代，意为“部分地搭在某物之上”。画面是一块布或木板越过另一物的边缘搭上去。

items.en: The single verb overlap appears, meaning 'to lay so as to cover part of something else'. It is formed by reversing the phrase: over + lap.
items.cn: 合为一体的动词 overlap 出现于 1726 年，意为“铺盖住另一物的一部分”。它由短语的词序调转而来：over + lap。

items.en: The noun overlap is recorded, first as the act of overlapping and then as the part that is shared.
items.cn: 名词 overlap 记录于 1813 年，先指“重叠这个动作”，后指“被共用的那部分”。

items.en: Technical use spreads: overlapping boards in shipbuilding, overlapping strata in geology, overlapping genes in genetics, and overlapping segments in phonology.
items.cn: 技术用法扩散开来：造船中的搭接板、地质学中的重叠地层、遗传学中的重叠基因、音系学中的重叠音段。

items.en: The figurative senses dominate now: overlapping interests, overlapping duties, and a scheduled overlap between two job holders. The physical strip remains the model for all of them.
items.cn: 如今占主导的是引申义：兴趣重叠、职责重叠、两任岗位之间的交接重叠期。那条物理上的共用带子仍是所有用法的模型。

note.en: The first group is about shape: over- words that do not mean sharing a zone. The second is about meaning: words for things that meet, cross, or repeat.
note.cn: 第一组看外形：同样带 over- 却不表示“共用一块区域”的词。第二组看词义：表示相接、相交或重复的词。

entries.definition: to lie over or on top of something, especially in layers of rock. It stresses one layer covering another, not a shared strip.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在……之上，尤指岩层。它强调一层盖住另一层，而不是共用一条带子。

entries.definition: to cover the surface of something with a layer, or the layer itself. The covering can be complete, while overlap is only partial.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物表面覆上一层，或指那一层本身。覆盖可以是完全的，而 overlap 只是部分的。

entries.definition: to load too much, or an excessive load. It shares the over- prefix but has nothing to do with shared area.
entries.definitionCN: 超载；装载过多。它同样带 over-，但与“共用区域”无关。

entries.definition: to look down on something from above, or to fail to notice it. Its over- is about position or neglect, not coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 俯瞰；忽视。它的 over- 表示位置或忽略，而不是覆盖。

entries.definition: to happen at the same time or occupy the same space exactly. It stresses simultaneous or identical position; overlap stresses a shared part.
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生，或完全占据同一空间。它强调同时或位置完全一致；overlap 强调“共有一部分”。

entries.definition: to cross or cut through each other, or to share common elements in set theory. Crossing produces a line or point; overlapping produces an area.
entries.definitionCN: 相交、交叉，或在集合论中有共同元素。交叉产生的是线或点，重叠产生的是面积。

entries.definition: to make an exact copy, or an exact copy itself. Complete sameness is the point, whereas overlap allows each side to keep something of its own.
entries.definitionCN: 复制；完全相同的副本。重点在“完全一样”，而重叠允许双方各自保留一部分。

entries.definition: to place one image or layer on top of another so that both remain visible. It is the technical cousin of the printing sense of overlap.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个影像或一层叠在另一层上，且两者都仍然可见。它是 overlap 印刷义的技术近亲。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on sound and spelling, then three abstract images for the idea of a shared strip.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个读音与拼写挂钩，再用三个抽象画面记住“共用一条带子”这个观念。

normal.en: lap is the knee: a book lies across your lap. Over-lap is one thing lying across another, sharing a strip.
normal.cn: lap 是“膝上”：书横放在膝上。over-lap 就是一物横搭在另一物上，共用一条带子。

normal.en: The verb is stressed at the back, the noun at the front: overLAP the sheets, but close the OVERlap. The heavier stress marks the action.
normal.cn: 动词重音在后，名词重音在前：overLAP 两张纸，但收拢 OVERlap。重音落在动作上。

normal.en: Hear the hyphen: over-lap means crossing the edge and lapping onto the other side.
normal.cn: 想象那个连字符：over-lap 就是越过边缘、搭到另一侧去。

normal.en: Picture a Venn diagram: the dark lens in the middle is the overlap, and both circles can point at it.
normal.cn: 想一个维恩图：中间那块深色透镜就是重叠部分，两个圆都能指向它。

normal.en: Shift change at a factory: the ten minutes when both crews are on the floor is the overlap.
normal.cn: 工厂交接班：两个班组同时站在车间里的那十分钟，就是 overlap。

abstract.en: Overlap is not similarity. It is a real shared interval that both sides can occupy at once.
abstract.cn: 重叠不是“相似”。它是一段双方都能同时占用的真实共用区间。

abstract.en: Cooperation starts in the overlap: the small zone of shared interest is the only ground on which two plans can be signed.
abstract.cn: 合作从重叠处开始：那一小块共同利益，是两个计划唯一能签字的地面。

abstract.en: Shared time is the one resource that cannot be returned. If two things overlap, they must be carried together.
abstract.cn: 共用的时间是无法退还的资源。两件事一旦重叠，就只能一起承担。

examples.en: The two circles overlap, and the shaded lens is where both claims hold.
examples.cn: 两个圆重叠，阴影的透镜形区域就是两种主张都成立的地方。

examples.en: Her new job overlaps with the old one for a month, which is enough time to hand over the files.
examples.cn: 她的新工作与旧工作有一个月的重叠期，足够交接文件。

examples.en: When the duties of two departments overlap, someone has to decide who answers the phone.
examples.cn: 当两个部门的职责重叠时，总得有人决定谁来接电话。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 over 记成“越过、在上”，lap 记成“搭、叠”：越过边界搭上一块，就是重叠。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（越过、在上）+ lap（搭叠）→ 部分重叠；重叠部分、重叠量

root: over（在上、越过）+ lap（搭、折叠）；lap 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with two surfaces sharing a strip, move the same strip through time and then through abstract ranges and duties, then name the strip and measure it, and end with the two technical uses where the strip is deliberate: printing layers and a job handover.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“两块表面共用一条带子”开始，把同一条带子依次移到时间、抽象范围与职责上，再把它名词化并加以度量，最后落到两种刻意安排的带子：印刷叠层与岗位交接。

core.en: Two sheets laid across each other, leaving one darker shared band
core.cn: 两张错开叠放的薄片，留下一条颜色更深的共用带

branches.en: Physical sharing: two surfaces cover the same patch.
branches.cn: 物理共用：两块表面覆盖同一片区域。

branches.en: Time sharing: an accidental clash of schedules, or a deliberate handover window.
branches.cn: 时间共用：日程的意外相撞，或刻意留出的交接窗口。

branches.en: Abstract sharing: interests that meet, and duties that claim the same task.
branches.cn: 抽象共用：相交的兴趣，以及争夺同一任务的两份职责。

branches.en: The strip named, then the strip measured as a proportion.
branches.cn: 先给这条带子命名，再把它度量成一个比例。

branches.en: Literal layering: ink or film pressed across another layer, darkening the shared band.
branches.cn: 字面叠层：油墨或胶片压过另一层，使共用带变深。

intro.en: Overlap sits in the huge over- family and the small lap family. Both halves are native English, so there is no Latin root here.
intro.cn: overlap 属于庞大的 over- 词族，也属于小小的 lap 词族。两半都是英语本族词，因此这里没有拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer, from Proto-Germanic *uber (PIE *uper); lap is a Germanic verb of uncertain deeper origin.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer，来自原始日耳曼语 *uber（原始印欧语 *uper）；lap 是一个日耳曼语动词，其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: to cover part of the same area, time, or range
items.meaningCN: 部分覆盖同一区域、时段或范围
items.example: The two schedules overlap on Friday.
items.exampleCN: 两份日程在周五重叠。

items.structure: same compound used as a noun
items.meaning: the shared part; the extent of sharing
items.example: The overlap is only ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 重叠部分只有百分之十。

items.meaning: sharing part of the same area or range
items.example: The two overlapping claims caused a dispute.
items.exampleCN: 两项重叠的主张引发了争议。

items.meaning: laid partly over something else
items.meaningCN: 被部分覆盖的；交叠起来的
items.example: The overlapped boards kept the rain out.
items.exampleCN: 交叠搭接的木板挡住了雨。

items.meaning: sharing no area or range at all
items.example: The two groups are nonoverlapping.
items.exampleCN: 这两个群体完全没有重叠。

items.meaning: across, above, beyond, or too much
items.example: Overhead, overland, overcharge.
items.exampleCN: 头顶的、陆路的、多收钱。

items.meaning: to fold or lay one thing over another
items.meaningCN: 折叠；把一物搭在另一物上
items.example: Lap the edge of the cloth over the seam.
items.exampleCN: 把布边搭过接缝。

items.meaning: a joint where one part falls short of covering another
items.meaningCN: 下搭接；欠重叠（工程中相接不足的接缝）
items.example: The engineer measured the underlap of the plates.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测量了钢板的欠重叠量。

items.meaning: in a way that shares part of the same area or range
items.example: The two terms are used overlappingly in the literature.
items.exampleCN: 文献中这两个术语被重叠地使用。

definition_zh: 海外的；国外的；在海外；向海外；（总称）海外地区
definition_en: located, happening, or living across the sea in a foreign country; also the foreign countries taken together as a region
core_image: 站在海岸线上，越过一条水带望向另一块陆地
scene: 港口堆场里，贴着外文标签的集装箱被吊上货轮。The shipping clerk wrote overseas on the destination line, and the crane lifted the last box toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 overseas 是「海外的、国外的」（第 1 个义项：位于国外）；句意：报关员在目的地一栏写下“海外”，吊机把最后一个箱子吊向大海。图中可辨识物件：集装箱、外文标签、吊机、货轮、报关单、海平线。

derivatives.zh: 海外的（较早的变体拼法）
驶往海外的；发往国外的

senses.title: Across the sea: located abroad
senses.definition: located or based in a country across the sea from the speaker's own
senses.definitionCN: 位于说话者本国之外、隔海相望的国家
senses.example: The company has three overseas branches.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有三家海外分公司。
senses.why: Over- means across or beyond, and sea is the water between the two shores. The reference point is always the speaker's own coast; what matters lies on the far side of the water.
senses.whyCN: over- 是“越过、在那边”，sea 是两岸之间的水。参照点始终是说话者自己这一侧的海岸，重要的事物在水的那一边。

senses.title: Coming from abroad
senses.definition: coming from or belonging to a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 来自外国或属于外国的
senses.example: Overseas visitors filled the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 海外游客挤满了博物馆。
senses.why: Here the direction reverses: the word marks not where the thing sits but where it came from. The sea is still the divider, only now the traffic crosses toward the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这里方向反了过来：词标记的不是事物所在之处，而是它来自何处。海仍是分界，只是人流物流朝说话者这一侧越过来。

senses.title: Abroad: the adverbial direction
senses.definition: to or in a country across the sea
senses.definitionCN: 到海外，或在海外
senses.example: She moved overseas after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后她移居海外。
senses.why: English lets the same compound serve as an adverb without adding -ly. The phrase names a path, and the path crosses water, so no separate adverb form was ever needed.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个复合词直接作副词，不必加 -ly。这个短语命名的是一条路径，而路径要越过水，因此从来不需要另造副词形式。

senses.title: The overseas as a named region
senses.definition: the countries beyond the sea, taken together as a region or sphere of activity
senses.definitionCN: 隔海之外的国家，作为一个地区或活动领域的总称
senses.example: Sales in the overseas grew faster than at home.
senses.exampleCN: 海外市场的销售增长快于国内。
senses.why: A locational phrase can be nominalized: the far side stops being a direction and becomes a territory with a name. Business and journalism then speak of the overseas as a single place with its own figures.
senses.whyCN: 方位短语可以名词化：那边不再是方向，而变成一块有名字的地盘。商业与新闻于是把“海外”当作一个有自己的数字的单一地方来谈。

senses.title: Foreign affairs: the official sphere
senses.definition: relating to a country's interests and activities beyond its borders
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一国国境之外的利益与活动
senses.example: The ministry handles overseas affairs.
senses.exampleCN: 该部负责海外事务。
senses.why: Bureaucracy names the foreign sphere as an adjective, and activities there become a department's remit. The word turns geography into an administrative portfolio.
senses.whyCN: 官僚体系用形容词命名对外领域，那边的活动就变成一个部门的职责。这个词把地理变成了一份行政分工。

senses.title: Living abroad: of people
senses.definition: of a person or community, living in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指个人或群体侨居外国
senses.example: Overseas Chinese communities kept the festival alive.
senses.exampleCN: 海外华人社群把这个节日保留了下来。
senses.why: For people the compound marks residence rather than origin: the person's daily life has moved to the far shore, even if the passport and the language have not.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，这个词标记的是“居住地”而不是“来源地”：此人的日常生活已经移到海那边，即使护照与语言没有跟着变。

senses.title: Military deployment beyond the sea
senses.definition: of troops or bases, stationed in a foreign country
senses.definitionCN: 指部队或基地驻扎在外国
senses.example: The unit served on overseas deployment for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队在海外部署了一年。
