senses.why: Armies inherit the maritime image even when they fly. Overseas still means outside the home territory, and the word keeps military language politely vague about which country is meant.
senses.whyCN: 军队即使坐飞机也继承了这个航海意象。overseas 仍指本国领土之外，同时让军事语言礼貌地含糊，不必点明是哪一个国家。

senses.title: Historical euphemism: the colonies
senses.definition: in British usage, a polite word for the colonies and dominions, especially in the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 英国用法中，对殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤见于 20 世纪早期
senses.example: Wartime posters promised work in the overseas dominions.
senses.exampleCN: 战时海报承诺在海外自治领有工作机会。
senses.why: Overseas let speakers avoid the word colony. Distance across water replaced a political relationship that many preferred not to name, which is how a neutral geographic term became an instrument of imperial tact.
senses.whyCN: overseas 让说话者避开“colony”这个词。隔海的距离替代了一段许多人不想点明的政治关系，于是一个中性的地理词变成了帝国辞令里的委婉工具。

intro.en: Overseas is a native English compound of over and sea. The word is transparent, but the deeper origin of sea itself is not certain.
intro.cn: overseas 是 over 与 sea 构成的英语本族复合词。词形透明，但 sea 本身的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: The older form oversea is recorded as an adjective and adverb meaning 'across the sea, on the other side of the sea'.
items.cn: 较早的形式 oversea 记录于 15 世纪，作形容词与副词，意为“隔海、在海的那一边”。

items.en: Overseas appears with the same meaning and eventually displaces oversea in most contexts. Both are simply over + sea.
items.cn: overseas 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，意义相同，最终在多数语境中取代 oversea。两者都只是 over + sea。

items.en: British imperial usage makes overseas a euphemism for the colonies and dominions, especially during the First World War.
items.cn: 英国帝国用语把 overseas 变成殖民地与自治领的委婉说法，尤在第一次世界大战期间。

items.en: The noun use is recorded: the overseas as the collective name for territories beyond the sea.
items.cn: 名词用法记录于 1919 年：the overseas 作为隔海之外领土的集合名称。

items.en: Trade, education, and the military keep the word busy: overseas market, overseas students, overseas deployment. The geographic frame stays neutral, which is exactly why it survives.
items.cn: 贸易、教育与军事让这个词持续活跃：海外市场、留学生、海外部署。它的地理框架保持中性，这也正是它存活下来的原因。

note.en: The first group collects over- words that look similar but do not mean across the sea. The second compares words for foreignness and distance.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 over-、外形相近却不表示“隔海”的词。第二组比较表示“异国、远方”的词。

entries.definition: to watch over and supervise work or people. It sounds almost the same but has no sea in it.
entries.definitionCN: 监督、管理工作的进行。读音几乎相同，但里面没有 sea。

entries.definition: larger than the standard size. It shares over- and the -size ending but means excess, not distance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过标准尺寸的。它同样带 over- 和 -size 结尾，但表示“过大”，而不是距离。

entries.definition: to express something more strongly than is justified. Its over- means too much, not across.
entries.definitionCN: 把话说得过头；夸大。它的 over- 表示“过分”，不是“越过”。

entries.definition: a loose garment worn over other clothes. It is over + all, and the plural -s can be mistaken for the -s of overseas.
entries.definitionCN: 穿在其他衣服外面的宽松工装。它是 over + all，复数 -s 容易被误当成 overseas 的 -s。

entries.definition: in or to a foreign country. It is only an adverb, while overseas can also be an adjective and a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在外国、到外国。它只能作副词，而 overseas 还能作形容词和名词。

entries.definition: belonging to a country other than one's own. It is the plain adjective and needs no sea, while overseas keeps the maritime image.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本国以外国家的。它是最朴素的形容词，不需要海；overseas 则保留了航海意象。

entries.definition: involving two or more nations. It stresses relations between states, while overseas stresses distance from home.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及两个或多个国家的。它强调国家之间的关系，overseas 强调与本土的距离。

entries.definition: away from the shore, especially of islands used for financial reasons. It is about distance from land, not about another country.
entries.definitionCN: 离岸的，尤指用于金融目的的海岛。它说的是离开陆地，而不是到另一个国家。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the over + sea picture, then three abstract images about distance and how it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 over + sea 画面的挂钩，再用三个关于距离及其用法的抽象画面。

normal.en: Say it as over-seas: over the seas, not over the sees. The plural seas are the water you cross.
normal.cn: 把它读成 over-seas：越过一片片海，而不是 over the sees。复数 seas 就是你越过的水。

normal.en: Look at a map: your finger starts on the home coast, crosses blue, and lands on another country. That finger path is overseas.
normal.cn: 看地图：手指从本国海岸出发，越过蓝色，落到另一个国家。那条手指路径就是 overseas。

normal.en: overseas students are students who crossed the sea to study; the sea is in the name, not in their luggage.
normal.cn: overseas students 是越过海来读书的学生；海在名字里，不在他们的行李里。

normal.en: The word has no -ly adverb form because it already works as an adverb: go overseas, live overseas.
normal.cn: 这个词没有 -ly 副词形式，因为它本身就能作副词：go overseas、live overseas。

normal.en: Overseas trade is trade that leaves the harbour; if the goods never touch water, the word still keeps the old picture.
normal.cn: overseas trade 是离开港口的贸易；即使货物从不碰水，这个词仍保留着旧画面。

abstract.en: Overseas is distance turned into a category: the far shore becomes an administrative box.
abstract.cn: overseas 是把距离变成一个分类：远岸被装进一个行政抽屉。

abstract.en: Every overseas is someone's home. The word marks the speaker's shore, not an absolute edge of the world.
abstract.cn: 每一个“海外”都是某些人的家。这个词标记的是说话者的海岸，而不是世界的绝对边缘。

abstract.en: The word is neutral geography doing political work: it can name a colony without saying colony.
abstract.cn: 这个词让中性的地理替政治干活：它可以指殖民地，却不必说出 colony。

examples.en: The firm opened an overseas office in Osaka last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天在大阪开设了海外办事处。

examples.en: Many overseas students work part-time while they improve their English.
examples.cn: 许多留学生在提高英语的同时做兼职。

examples.en: The letters went overseas by ship and took six weeks to arrive.
examples.cn: 这些信件经海路寄往海外，走了六周才到。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 over 记成“越过”，sea 记成“海”：越过海的那一边，就是海外。
dict_mnemonic.text: over（越过）+ sea（海）+ -s → 海外的、在海外；海外地区

root: over（越过）+ sea（海）；sea 是日耳曼语固有词，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow the direction of travel: first something sits on the far shore, then it comes toward the speaker, then the word becomes a path, a named region, an official portfolio, a way of living, a military station, and finally a polite imperial word for the colonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项顺着旅行的方向展开：先有东西位于远岸，再有东西朝说话者这边来，随后这个词变成一条路径、一块被命名的地区、一份官方职责、一种居住方式、一处军事驻地，最后成为帝国辞令里对殖民地的委婉说法。

core.en: A coastline, a band of water, and another land on the far side
core.cn: 一条海岸线、一条水带，以及水那边另一块陆地

branches.en: A place across the sea: the word locates something abroad.
branches.cn: 海那边的地方：这个词指某物位于国外。

branches.en: From a path to a place: the adverb of movement becomes a named region.
branches.cn: 从路径到地方：表示移动的副词变成一块被命名的地区。

branches.en: The official sphere: foreign affairs at a desk, and troops in the field.
branches.cn: 官方领域：办公桌上的对外事务，以及战场上的海外驻军。

branches.en: People: those who live and work across the sea.
branches.cn: 人：在海外生活与工作的那些人。

branches.en: Origin and old tongue: goods that come from across the sea, and the older British label for the colonies.
branches.cn: 来源与旧称：从海那边来的货物，以及英国旧时对殖民地的说法。

intro.en: Overseas is built from the over- prefix and the sea family. The items below include both true relatives and the nearest sea compounds, so the boundary of the family is visible.
intro.cn: overseas 由 over- 前缀和 sea 词族构成。下面既有真正的同族词，也有最接近的海事复合词，以便看清词族的边界。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: over is Old English ofer (PIE *uper), and sea is Old English sæ, from Proto-Germanic *saiwiz, whose deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：over 是古英语 ofer（原始印欧语 *uper），sea 是古英语 sæ，来自原始日耳曼语 *saiwiz，其更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: across the sea; in or from a foreign country
items.meaningCN: 隔海；在海外或来自海外
items.example: They went overseas in 1998.
items.exampleCN: 他们 1998 年去了海外。

items.meaning: the earlier adjective and adverb, now mostly replaced
items.meaningCN: 较早的形容词与副词形式，现已多被取代
items.example: An oversea cable was laid in 1866.
items.exampleCN: 一条海底电缆于 1866 年铺设。

items.meaning: across, beyond, above
items.example: Overland travel, overboard, overflight.
items.exampleCN: 陆路旅行、落水、飞越。

items.meaning: the salt water that covers most of the earth
items.meaningCN: 覆盖地球大部分区域的咸水
items.example: The sea was calm that morning.
items.exampleCN: 那天早晨海面平静。

items.meaning: toward the sea
items.example: The seaward window caught the wind.
items.exampleCN: 朝海的窗户迎进了风。

items.meaning: carried by sea
items.example: Seaborne trade recovered slowly.
items.exampleCN: 海运贸易恢复缓慢。

items.meaning: working or traveling on the sea
items.example: A seafaring family kept the old charts.
items.exampleCN: 一个航海世家保存着旧海图。

items.meaning: away from the shore; of financial islands
items.meaningCN: 离岸的；金融意义上的离岸
items.example: The funds were held offshore.
items.exampleCN: 资金存放在离岸账户。

items.meaning: crossing an ocean
items.example: A transoceanic flight takes twelve hours.
items.exampleCN: 跨洋飞行需要十二小时。

definition_zh: 面板；镶板；控制面板；专家小组；陪审团名单；（漫画）分格；固定样本组
definition_en: a flat rectangular piece fitted into a frame or surface; also a group of people selected to sit together and give opinions or make decisions
core_image: 一块绷在框架里的方形板，也可以是一群人选出来坐到同一张长桌后面
scene: 演播室里，四位专家坐在长桌后。A square panel of lights came on above the table, and the host asked the four experts beneath it to begin.
sceneCN: 这里 panel 是「嵌在框架里的平板、灯板」（第 1 个义项：嵌在框架里的平板）；句意：长桌上方一块方形灯板亮起，主持人请坐在它下面的四位专家开始讨论。图中可辨识物件：长桌、四把椅子、专家名牌、方形灯板、麦克风。

pos.zh: （选出的）专家小组；评审团；讨论组

forms.label: 过去式／过去分词（英式拼写）
过去式／过去分词（美式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 镶板材料；镶板工程（美式拼写）
分面板；子面板；下级小组

senses.title: A flat piece fitted into a frame
senses.definition: a usually rectangular piece of wood, glass, or metal that forms part of a surface or is set into a frame
senses.definitionCN: 通常为矩形的木、玻璃或金属板，构成某个表面的一部分，或嵌在框架里
senses.example: One panel of the door was cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 门上有一块镶板裂了。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a square piece of cloth. A piece cut to fit a frame keeps that shape, so the first modern sense is simply a flat rectangle inserted into a larger surface.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一块方形的布。裁好嵌进框架的一块仍保留那个形状，因此最早的现代义就是“插进更大表面里的一块平板”。

senses.title: The surface you operate: control panel
senses.titleCN: 你操作的那块面：控制面板
senses.definition: a flat surface on a machine or device that holds the controls, dials, or screens
senses.definitionCN: 机器或装置上集中安放控制键、旋钮或屏幕的平面
senses.example: The pilot checked the panel before takeoff.
senses.exampleCN: 起飞前飞行员检查了仪表板。
senses.why: A fitted board is a natural place to mount switches. Once the board carries the controls, the object becomes the interface, and the panel is what the hand reaches for.
senses.whyCN: 嵌装好的板面天然适合安装开关。一旦这块板承载了控制装置，它就成了人机接口，“面板”也就成了手要伸向的那块地方。

senses.title: A selected group at one table
senses.titleCN: 被选出来坐在一起的一组人
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to discuss a subject, judge a competition, or advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 被选出来讨论某个议题、评审比赛或提供建议的一组人
senses.example: A panel of judges will review the entries.
senses.exampleCN: 一个评审小组将审阅参赛作品。
senses.why: The group sense grows from a written list of names: a panel was first the sheet on which chosen names were written. The paper gave its name to the people listed on it.
senses.whyCN: “一组人”的义项来自一张写有名字的名单：panel 最初指写着被选中者名字的那张纸。纸的名字后来转移到了纸上所列的人身上。

senses.title: The jury list, and the jury itself
senses.titleCN: 陪审员名单，以及陪审团
senses.definition: the list of people summoned to serve on a jury, or the jury so formed
senses.definitionCN: 被传唤担任陪审员者的名单，或由此组成的陪审团
senses.example: The clerk read the panel aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员在法庭上宣读了陪审员名单。
senses.why: In law the sheet of names came first: the panel was the roll. Then the word shifted to the body of people on the roll, which is the same paper-to-people transfer seen in the expert sense.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，先有那张名单：panel 是名册。随后词义转到名册上的人，这与“专家组”义项中“纸→人”的转移完全相同。

senses.title: A frame in a comic strip
senses.definition: one framed picture or box in a comic strip or graphic novel
senses.definitionCN: 连环画或图像小说中被边框围住的一幅画或一格
senses.example: The final panel shows the empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一格画的是空荡荡的街道。
senses.why: Each comic image is literally a rectangle drawn inside a border, a panel fitted into the page. The printing term for a bordered block transferred to the art form built out of such blocks.
senses.whyCN: 漫画的每一幅画就是画在边框里的一个矩形，即嵌进页面的一块板。印刷业对“带框区块”的叫法，转移到了由这种区块构成的画种上。

senses.title: A solar panel: a board that collects
senses.titleCN: 太阳能板：一块收集能量的板
senses.definition: one of the flat modules that make up a solar array, converting sunlight into electricity
senses.definitionCN: 组成太阳能阵列的平坦模块之一，把阳光转化为电能
senses.example: The roof holds twelve solar panels.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶装了十二块太阳能板。
senses.why: The object is again a flat rectangle mounted into a frame, this time a roof or a rack. What changed is the function: the board no longer covers, it collects.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是嵌在框架（屋顶或支架）里的一块平板。改变的是功能：这块板不再用于遮盖，而是用于收集。

senses.title: A panel show: guests as a group
senses.titleCN: panel show：嘉宾作为一组出场
senses.definition: in broadcasting, a programme in which a group of guests discuss or compete
senses.definitionCN: 广播或电视中由一组嘉宾讨论或竞赛的节目
senses.example: The comedy panel show runs every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这档喜剧小组节目每周五播出。
senses.why: Television keeps the legal and expert group but changes the setting: the panel is now chosen for entertainment, and the group itself becomes the format of the programme.
senses.whyCN: 电视保留了法律与专家义里的“一组人”，却换了场景：panel 现在是为娱乐而挑选的，这一组人本身就成了节目的形式。

senses.title: A fixed sample followed over time
senses.titleCN: 长期追踪的固定样本组
senses.definition: in research, a group of the same people or households surveyed repeatedly over time
senses.definitionCN: 研究中被反复调查、长期追踪的同一批人或家庭
senses.example: The household panel has been interviewed every year since 1990.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭样本组自 1990 年以来每年接受访谈。
senses.why: A panel here is a list that is deliberately kept closed: the same names stay on the roll so that changes can be measured. The legal roll of names becomes a scientific instrument.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 panel 是一份刻意保持封闭的名单：同一批名字始终留在名册上，以便测量变化。法律上的名册于是变成了科学工具。

intro.en: Panel is a small French word for a piece of cloth that grew into a word for boards, lists, and groups. The date of the Latin base is old, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: panel 本是法语里指一块布的小词，后来长成指板、名单与群体的词。其拉丁语基础年代久远，但更早来源不确定。

items.en: Panel is recorded meaning 'a piece of cloth, especially a square'. It comes from Old French panel, a diminutive of pan 'piece of cloth'.
items.cn: panel 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，意为“一块布，尤指方形的布”。它来自古法语 panel，是 pan“一块布”的指小形式。

items.en: The legal sense appears: the panel is the schedule or roll of jurors. The sheet of paper is named first; the jury named on it follows later.
items.cn: 法律义出现：panel 指陪审员的名单或名册。先命名那张纸，纸上所列的陪审团随后才被这样称呼。

items.en: The sense 'group of experts' is recorded, again by transfer from a list of selected names to the people themselves.
items.cn: “专家组”义记录于 16 世纪 70 年代，同样是“被选中者的名单”转移到“这些人本身”。

items.en: The wooden architectural sense becomes common: a panel is a board set into wainscot or a door. The verb appears in the 15c. as empanel 'to enter on a roll' and in the 1630s as 'to fit with panels'.
items.cn: 建筑木作义在 1600 年前后普及：panel 是嵌进护墙板或门里的木板。动词 15 世纪出现，作 empanel“列入名册”；17 世纪 30 年代又有“装镶板”义。

items.en: Technology multiplies the board: control panel, instrument panel, solar panel. Media adds the comic panel and the panel show; social science adds the survey panel.
items.cn: 技术让“板”大量增殖：控制面板、仪表板、太阳能板。传媒加上漫画分格与小组节目；社会科学加上调查样本组。

note.en: The first group separates near spellings; the second compares words for organised groups of people.
note.cn: 第一组把形近词分开；第二组比较表示“有组织的一组人”的词。

entries.definition: relating to punishment, especially under the law. One letter differs, and its root is poena 'penalty', not pannus 'cloth'.
entries.definitionCN: 与刑罚有关的，尤指法律上的。只差一个字母，其词根是 poena“惩罚”，不是 pannus“布”。

entries.definition: sudden uncontrolled fear. It looks close but comes from Pan, the Greek god whose sudden appearances caused alarm.
entries.definitionCN: 突如其来的失控恐惧。外形相近，但来自希腊神 Pan——他的突然出现会引发惊惶。

entries.definition: the boards that line a wall, or the work of fitting them. It is the noun from panel, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 墙面上的镶板，或安装镶板的工程。它是 panel 派生的名词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a member of a panel. The -ist suffix marks a person, so it is a true derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 小组或评审组的一员。-ist 后缀标记人，因此它是真正的派生词。

entries.definition: a formally appointed group that meets to decide or manage. It has authority and procedure; a panel is often advisory or judging.
entries.definitionCN: 正式任命、开会决策或管理的团体。它有权力与程序；panel 常是咨询性或评审性的。

entries.definition: the group of people who decide a case in court. A panel can be the list from which the jury is drawn.
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上裁决案件的一组人。panel 可以指从中抽取陪审员的那份名单。

entries.definition: the group that governs a company or institution. It is permanent and powerful, while a panel is usually assembled for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 治理公司或机构的团体。它是常设且有实权的，而 panel 通常为某项任务临时组成。

entries.definition: a meeting or place for open discussion, often with an audience. It stresses exchange; a panel stresses the few selected speakers.
entries.definitionCN: 公开讨论的会议或场所，常有听众。它强调交流；panel 强调被选出的少数发言者。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the board and the table, then three abstract images about selection and framing.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕“板”和“长桌”的挂钩，再用三个关于“遴选与取景”的抽象画面。

normal.en: panel and pane: a window pane is a sheet of glass, and a panel is a sheet fitted into a frame. Same shape, same idea.
normal.cn: panel 与 pane：窗玻璃是一整片，panel 是嵌进框架的一片。形状相同，想法也相同。

normal.en: A control panel is where your fingers walk: buttons arranged on one flat board.
normal.cn: 控制面板是手指行走的地方：按钮排在同一块平板上。

normal.en: Think of a talk show: four chairs behind one long desk. The desk makes the group a panel.
normal.cn: 想一场脱口秀：一张长桌后四把椅子。那张长桌把这一组人变成 panel。

normal.en: A jury panel is first a list on paper, then the people on the paper. Paper first, people second.
normal.cn: 陪审团 panel 先是纸上的一份名单，然后才是名单上的人。先纸，后人。

normal.en: Solar panels are panels that stopped covering walls and started collecting light.
normal.cn: 太阳能板是不再盖墙、改去收集光的面板。

abstract.en: A panel is a frame that decides what counts: the board cuts a piece out of a larger surface and makes it the unit.
abstract.cn: panel 是一个决定“什么算数”的框：它从更大的表面里切出一块，让这块成为单位。

abstract.en: A panel of people is a list made visible: selection is the real subject, and the table is only where the list sits.
abstract.cn: 由人组成的 panel 是一份被看见的名单：真正的主角是“遴选”，长桌只是名单落座的地方。

abstract.en: Every panel hides the rest of the wall. What is outside the frame is as important as what is inside.
abstract.cn: 每一块面板都遮住了墙的其余部分。框外之物与框内之物同样重要。

examples.en: The inspector opened the control panel and found a loose wire.
examples.cn: 检查员打开控制面板，发现一根松动的电线。

examples.en: A panel of three teachers will interview the candidates.
examples.cn: 一个由三位教师组成的小组将面试候选人。

examples.en: The survey follows the same panel of families for ten years.
examples.cn: 这项调查对同一批家庭样本追踪十年。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 pan 记成“一片”，-el 记成“小块”：一片裁好的方板；一群被写进同一张名单的人，也像排在同一块板上。
dict_mnemonic.text: pan（一片布、一片） + -el（指小）→ 嵌板、面板 → 名单 → 坐在名单上的一组人

root: 古法语 panel（一块布）< 通俗拉丁 *pannellus < 拉丁 pannus“布片”；pannus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one object and one list: a fitted square of cloth or wood becomes a control surface, a comic frame, and a solar module; meanwhile a roll of selected names becomes a jury, an expert group, a broadcast format, and a research sample.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项沿着“一块板”和“一份名单”两条线展开：裁好嵌进去的方板变成控制面、漫画格与太阳能模块；而被选中者的名册则变成陪审团、专家组、节目形式与研究样本。

core.en: A square board set into a frame, and a sheet of names laid on a table
core.cn: 一块嵌进框架的方形板，以及一张铺在桌上的名单

branches.en: The board and its working face: a fitted rectangle becomes the place where controls sit.
branches.cn: 板与它的工作面：一块嵌好的矩形变成安放控制装置的地方。

branches.en: The selected group: experts at a table, then guests arranged as a programme format.
branches.cn: 被选出的一组：长桌后的专家，随后被编排成节目形式的嘉宾组。

branches.en: The roll of names: jurors summoned by a list, and a sample kept on a list for years.
branches.cn: 名册：按名单传唤的陪审员，以及多年保留在同一名单上的样本。

branches.en: The framed rectangle as an artistic unit: one bordered picture in a comic strip.
branches.cn: 作为艺术单位的带框矩形：连环画中被边框围住的一格。

branches.en: A board that collects: a solar panel turning sunlight into current.
branches.cn: 一块收集能量的板：把阳光变成电流的太阳能板。

intro.en: Panel has a small but clear family: the base word, its person noun, its material noun, and a few prefixed or compound forms.
intro.cn: panel 的词族不大但很清楚：基词、指人的名词、指材料的名词，以及几个加前缀或复合的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is pannus 'cloth, rag', with a Vulgar Latin diminutive *pannellus. The further origin of pannus is uncertain, so no deeper root is asserted here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 pannus“布、破布”，其通俗拉丁语指小形式为 *pannellus。pannus 的更早来源不确定，因此这里不强行给出更深词根。

items.meaning: a piece of cloth; later a fitted board or a listed group
items.meaningCN: 一块布；后来指嵌板或名单上的一组人
items.example: The wall was divided into panels.
items.exampleCN: 墙面被分成一块块镶板。

items.meaning: a member of a panel
items.example: Each panelist had five minutes.
items.exampleCN: 每位小组成员有五分钟。

items.meaning: boards fitted to a wall; the work of fitting them
items.example: Oak paneling covered the hall.
items.exampleCN: 橡木镶板覆盖了大厅墙面。

items.meaning: fitted with panels
items.example: A panelled study faced the garden.
items.exampleCN: 一间镶板书房朝向花园。

items.meaning: a smaller panel within a larger one; a subordinate group
items.meaningCN: 大面板中的分面板；下级小组
items.example: The subpanel reports to the main committee.
items.exampleCN: 下级小组向主委员会汇报。

items.meaning: to enter a person on a jury roll; to form a panel
items.meaningCN: 把某人列入陪审员名册；组成小组
items.example: The court empanelled twelve jurors.
items.exampleCN: 法庭组成了十二人的陪审团。

items.meaning: a piece of cloth (the source of panel)
items.example: Pan in Old French meant a patch of cloth.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 pan 指一块布片。

items.meaning: a single sheet of glass in a frame
items.example: The ball broke a pane of the window.
items.exampleCN: 球打碎了窗户的一块玻璃。

items.meaning: a research design that re-surveys the same sample
items.meaningCN: 对同一样本重复调查的研究设计
items.example: The panel study tracked income for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 该样本研究追踪收入达十年。

latinEntries.meaning: cloth, rag, a piece of fabric
latinEntries.example: Pannus is the base of French pan and English panel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pannus 是法语 pan 与英语 panel 的基础词。

latinEntries.meaning: a small piece of cloth (reconstructed Vulgar Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一小块布（重构的通俗拉丁语形式）
latinEntries.example: Vulgar Latin *pannellus led to Old French panel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 通俗拉丁语 *pannellus 演变为古法语 panel。

definition_zh: 范式；典范；样板；（语言学）词形变化表；（科学哲学）理论框架
definition_en: a model or pattern; in grammar, the full set of forms a word can take; in science, the shared assumptions within which research is done
core_image: 一块竖起的样板，旁边整齐排着同一套变化的所有形态
scene: 语言学课堂上，黑板上画着一整张动词变位表。The teacher tapped the whole paradigm with her pointer and said that every cell showed one form of the same verb.
sceneCN: 这里 paradigm 是「词形变化表」（第 1 个义项：所有形态并排展示）；句意：老师用教鞭敲着整张词形变化表，说每一格都是同一个动词的一种形式。图中可辨识物件：黑板、变位表格、粉笔、教鞭、讲台。

pos.zh: （语言学）词形变化表；词形变化系统

collocations.zh: 范式转移；思维框架的根本转变

derivatives.zh: 范式的；典范的；词形变化上的
以范式的方式；作为典范地

senses.title: The grammar table: all forms side by side
senses.titleCN: 语法表：所有形态并排展示
senses.definition: in grammar, a table showing all the inflected forms of a word, such as a verb's persons and tenses
senses.definitionCN: 语法中展示一个词全部屈折形式的表格，如动词的人称与时态
senses.example: The students copied the paradigm of the verb into their notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把那个动词的变位表抄进笔记本。
senses.why: Greek paradeigma meant a pattern shown beside something. A grammar table does exactly that: it sets every form of one word next to the others so the pattern becomes visible at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 paradeigma 意为“摆在旁边给人看的样板”。语法表正是如此：把一个词的所有形态并排摆开，让模式一眼可见。

senses.title: The inflectional system behind the table
senses.titleCN: 表格背后的词形变化系统
senses.definition: the whole system of inflections that a class of words follows
senses.definitionCN: 某一类词所遵循的整套屈折变化系统
senses.example: English nouns have a much simpler paradigm than Latin nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 英语名词的变格系统比拉丁语名词简单得多。
senses.why: Once the table is learned, the table stands for the rule. Linguists speak of the paradigm as the system, not the paper, because the same pattern can be reproduced for any word of the class.
senses.whyCN: 表格一旦被掌握，表就代表了规则。语言学家说的 paradigm 是系统而不是那张纸，因为同一模式可以为该类词中的任何一词重现。

senses.title: A model worth copying
senses.definition: a model, example, or pattern that others are expected to follow
senses.definitionCN: 供他人效仿的模范、例子或模式
senses.example: Her career became a paradigm for young scientists.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职业生涯成了年轻科学家的样板。
senses.why: The Greek word already carried the sense of an example set before a learner. The table is a pattern to copy, so the word naturally extends from grammar to any model held up for imitation.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词本就带有“摆在学习者面前的例子”之义。表格是可以照抄的模式，因此这个词自然从语法扩展到任何被举起来供人效仿的样板。

senses.title: Kuhn's scientific paradigm
senses.definition: in the philosophy of science, the set of shared assumptions, methods, and exemplars within which a scientific community works
senses.definitionCN: 科学哲学中，一个科学共同体工作其间的共同假设、方法与范例的总和
senses.example: Newtonian mechanics was the ruling paradigm for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿力学在两个世纪里是占统治地位的范式。
senses.why: Thomas Kuhn adopted the word in 1962 because a scientific community, like a language class, works from a shared set of exemplary solutions. The pattern is not written on a table but held in common, and that is what makes normal research possible.
senses.whyCN: 托马斯·库恩在 1962 年采用这个词，因为科学共同体就像一个语言班级，依靠一套共同的范例解法工作。这个模式不写在表上，而是被共同持有，正是它让常规研究成为可能。

senses.title: The framework of an era
senses.definition: the dominant set of ideas and assumptions of a period or field, which makes some questions askable and others invisible
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期或领域占主导的观念与假设集合，它决定哪些问题可被提出、哪些则不可见
senses.example: The paradigm of endless growth shaped city planning for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 无限增长的范式塑造了城市规划数十年。
senses.why: A shared framework does more than guide work: it decides what counts as a problem. That is why the word can name the invisible boundary of an age, not just a method inside it.
senses.whyCN: 共同的框架不只是指导工作：它决定什么才算“问题”。因此这个词可以命名一个时代的无形边界，而不只是时代内部的一种方法。

senses.title: A business or technological paradigm
senses.definition: the established way an industry produces value, especially before a disruptive change
senses.definitionCN: 一个行业创造价值的既定方式，尤指在颠覆性变化之前
senses.example: Subscription pricing became the new paradigm for software.
senses.exampleCN: 订阅制定价成了软件业的新范式。
senses.why: Business borrows the scientific word for the same reason: a whole industry can share one model of how money is made. A shift in that model rearranges winners and losers, not just methods.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用这个科学词，理由相同：整个行业可以共用一个“钱如何赚”的模式。模式一变，赢家与输家就会重排，而不只是方法更换。

senses.title: A programming paradigm
senses.definition: a fundamental style of programming, such as object-oriented or functional programming, that shapes how problems are expressed
senses.definitionCN: 编程的根本风格，如面向对象或函数式编程，它决定问题如何被表达
senses.example: The course moves from procedural to object-oriented paradigms.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从过程式范式过渡到面向对象范式。
senses.why: A programming style is a grammar of solutions: it tells you what a problem looks like before you solve it. The word fits because the style is learned as a pattern and then applied to new cases.
senses.whyCN: 编程风格是一套“解法的语法”：它在解题之前就规定问题长什么样。这个词之所以适用，是因为这种风格作为模式被学会，再套用到新个例上。

senses.title: The paradigm case in philosophy
senses.definition: an example that is taken as the clearest instance of a concept and against which other cases are judged
senses.definitionCN: 被当作某概念最清晰实例、并用来衡量其他个案的例子
senses.example: A clear case of knowledge serves as the paradigm case in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 一个清晰的知识实例成为这场争论中的典型个案。
senses.why: Here the model is a single case rather than a table. Philosophy needs one uncontested instance to anchor a concept, and that instance is held up beside doubtful cases exactly as the Greek word suggests.
senses.whyCN: 这里作为样板的是单个案例而不是表格。哲学需要一个无争议的实例来锚定概念，这个实例被摆到可疑案例旁边，正是希腊词字面上的做法。

intro.en: Paradigm is Greek in origin and reached English through Late Latin. Its parts are well attested; the modern scientific sense is a deliberate twentieth-century borrowing.
intro.cn: paradigm 源自希腊语，经晚期拉丁语进入英语。其构词成分有明确记载；现代科学义是 20 世纪有意的借用。

items.en: Paradigm is recorded in English meaning 'an example, a model'. It comes from Late Latin paradigma, from Greek paradeigma 'pattern, model, sample'.
items.cn: paradigm 于 15 世纪晚期进入英语，意为“例子、模范”。它来自晚期拉丁语 paradigma，再上溯希腊语 paradeigma“模式、样板、样本”。

items.en: Paradeigma is formed from para- 'beside' and the verb deiknynai 'to show, point out'. The literal picture is something shown beside something else so that it can be compared.
items.cn: paradeigma 由 para-“在旁边”与动词 deiknynai“展示、指出来”构成。字面画面是把某物摆在另一物旁边，以便比较。

items.en: Deiknynai goes back to PIE *deik- 'to show, point out', the same family as English token and the deictic words that point at things. The asterisk marks a reconstructed root.
items.cn: deiknynai 上溯原始印欧语 *deik-“展示、指出”，与英语 token 以及表示“指指点点”的指示词同族。星号表示这是重构词根。

items.en: The grammatical sense is recorded: a paradigm is the table of all the inflected forms of a word. The table is the model shown beside the word it describes.
items.cn: 语法义记录于 16 世纪后期：paradigm 是一个词全部屈折形式的表格。表格就是摆在所描述之词旁边的样板。

items.en: Thomas Kuhn's The Structure of Scientific Revolutions makes paradigm a name for a scientific community's shared framework. Kuhn later said he preferred 'disciplinary matrix', but the popular sense stuck.
items.cn: 托马斯·库恩《科学革命的结构》使 paradigm 成为“科学共同体共享框架”的名称。库恩后来说他更愿意用 disciplinary matrix，但流行开来的仍是 paradigm。

note.en: The first group is a para- family that is easy to confuse; the second compares words for models and frameworks.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混淆的 para- 词族；第二组比较表示“样板与框架”的词。

entries.definition: a distinct section of writing. Its para- means beside, and the second part is graphein 'to write', not deiknynai.
entries.definitionCN: 文章中的一个独立段落。它的 para- 是“在旁边”，后半是 graphein“写”，不是 deiknynai。

entries.definition: a statement that seems to contradict itself. Its second part is doxa 'opinion', so it is 'beside opinion', not 'shown beside'.
entries.definitionCN: 看似自相矛盾的说法。后半是 doxa“意见”，所以是“与意见相悖”，不是“摆在旁边展示”。

entries.definition: loss of movement in the body. Its para- means beside or beyond, and lysis means loosening, a medical compound far from paradigm.
entries.definitionCN: 身体失去运动能力。它的 para- 是“在旁边、超出”，lysis 是“松开”，这一医学复合词与 paradigm 相距很远。

entries.definition: a person trained to give emergency medical care alongside doctors. The para- means alongside, and the second part is medical.
entries.definitionCN: 与医生并肩提供急救护理的人。para- 是“并肩”，后半是 medical。

entries.definition: a simplified representation or an example to follow. It is the broad everyday word; paradigm adds the idea of a whole framework shared by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 简化的表征，或可供效仿的榜样。它是最宽泛的日常词；paradigm 增加了“一个群体共享的整套框架”之意。

entries.definition: the supporting structure or set of ideas that holds something together. It stresses structure, while paradigm stresses the exemplary pattern inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑结构，或把事物组织起来的一套观念。它强调结构，而 paradigm 强调结构内部的典范模式。

entries.definition: the original model from which copies are made, often in psychology or literature. It is more about an original than about a working community.
entries.definitionCN: 被复制所依据的原型，常用于心理学或文学。它更强调“原初”，而不是一个工作共同体。

entries.definition: a shaped pattern used to produce identical copies. It is concrete and often physical, while paradigm is usually conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制作相同副本的样板。它具体、常为实物，而 paradigm 通常是概念性的。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sound and the grammar table, then three abstract images about shared frameworks.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕读音与语法表的挂钩，再用三个关于“共享框架”的抽象画面。

normal.en: para- means beside, and -digm comes from showing: a paradigm is a sample shown beside the thing it explains.
normal.cn: para- 是“在旁边”，-digm 来自“展示”：paradigm 就是摆在被解释之物旁边的样本。

normal.en: Think of a Latin verb chart: amo, amas, amat down the page. That chart is a paradigm, and every form is a cell in it.
normal.cn: 想一张拉丁语动词表：amo、amas、amat 一路排下去。那张表就是 paradigm，每个形态是表里的一格。

normal.en: A paradigm shift is not a new answer to the old question; it is a new table on which the questions are written.
normal.cn: paradigm shift 不是给旧问题换新答案，而是换了一张写问题的表。

normal.en: Say it PARA-dime, not para-DIG-em: the stress is on the first syllable, like the pattern standing in front.
normal.cn: 读作 PARA-dime，而不是 para-DIG-em：重音在第一音节，就像样板立在最前面。

normal.en: Grammar first, science later: the word spent four centuries as a schoolroom table before Kuhn made it a theory of science.
normal.cn: 先有语法，后有科学：这个词在教室里当了几百年的变位表，之后库恩才把它变成科学理论。

abstract.en: A paradigm is a frame you cannot see while you are inside it. You notice it only when another frame appears beside it.
abstract.cn: 范式是你身处其中时看不见的框。只有当另一个框出现在旁边，你才注意到它。

abstract.en: Paradigms save thought by pre-deciding what a problem looks like; that saving is also their danger.
abstract.cn: 范式通过事先决定“问题长什么样”来节省思考；这种节省也正是它的危险。

abstract.en: Every paradigm is a table with missing cells: what a community never writes down is part of the pattern too.
abstract.cn: 每个范式都是一张有空格子的表：一个共同体从不写下的东西，也是模式的一部分。

examples.en: The textbook prints the paradigm of the noun at the top of each chapter.
examples.cn: 教科书在每章开头印出该名词的变格表。

examples.en: Kuhn argued that a paradigm shift is a change of the questions a field can ask.
examples.cn: 库恩认为，范式转移是一个领域“能问什么问题”的改变。

examples.en: Object-oriented programming is a paradigm, not a language.
examples.cn: 面向对象编程是一种范式，而不是一门语言。

dict_mnemonic.note: para- 记成“在旁边”，-digm 记成“展示”：把一整套样板摆在旁边给你照着做，就是范式。
dict_mnemonic.text: para（在旁边）+ deiknynai（展示）→ 摆在旁边的样板 → 词形表、典范、科学范式

root: 希腊 paradeigma“样板”，来自 para-（在旁边）+ deiknynai（展示，原始印欧语 *deik-）→ 晚期拉丁 paradigma → 英语 paradigm。

sensesIntro.en: The senses begin with a grammar table that shows every form of one word, move to the system behind that table, then to any model held up for copying, and finally to the large shared frameworks of science, an era, an industry, a programming style, and a single exemplary case.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从一张展示单词全部形态的语法表开始，转到表格背后的系统，再到任何被举起来供人照做的样板，最后扩展到科学、时代、行业、编程风格乃至单个典型个案这些大型共享框架。

core.en: A pattern set beside the thing it explains, so that every form can be seen at once
core.cn: 摆在被解释之物旁边的样板，让所有形态一次看全

branches.en: The table and the rule: a printed chart of forms, and the inflectional system it displays.
branches.cn: 表与规则：印着形态的表格，以及它所展示的屈折系统。

branches.en: A model worth copying: an example held up for others to follow.
branches.cn: 值得照做的样板：被举出来让别人跟随的例子。

branches.en: Shared assumptions: a scientific community's framework, and the invisible boundary of an era.
branches.cn: 共享假设：科学共同体的框架，以及一个时代的无形边界。

branches.en: Working styles: how an industry makes money, and how a programmer expresses a problem.
branches.cn: 工作风格：一个行业如何赚钱，以及程序员如何表达问题。

branches.en: The typical case: the clearest instance of a concept, used to judge other cases.
branches.cn: 典型个案：某概念最清晰的实例，用来衡量其他个案。

intro.en: Paradigm is a compound of two Greek parts, and its family is mostly Greek-derived: the adjective, the adverb, the shift, the case, and the verb of making something a pattern.
intro.cn: paradigm 由两个希腊成分构成，其词族多为希腊来源：形容词、副词、转移、个案，以及“使成范式”的动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin route is paradigma, a Late Latin borrowing of Greek paradeigma. Latin adds no new root; it only carries the Greek compound into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语环节是 paradigma，即晚期拉丁语对希腊语 paradeigma 的借用。拉丁语没有增加新词根，只是把这个希腊复合词送进法语和英语。

items.meaning: a pattern or model; a table of forms; a shared framework
items.meaningCN: 样板或模式；形态表；共享框架
items.example: The discovery broke the old paradigm.
items.exampleCN: 这一发现打破了旧范式。

items.meaning: serving as a model; relating to a paradigm or to inflection
items.meaningCN: 典范性的；与范式或词形变化有关的
items.example: Her response was paradigmatic of the school's method.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答是该学派方法的典型代表。

items.meaning: in a way that exemplifies a pattern
items.meaningCN: 以典范的方式；作为模式地
items.example: The case is paradigmatically a case of trust.
items.exampleCN: 这个案例在范式意义上正是一个信任案例。

items.meaning: a fundamental change in the shared framework of a field
items.meaningCN: 一个领域共享框架的根本改变
items.example: The internet caused a paradigm shift in retail.
items.exampleCN: 互联网引发了零售业的范式转移。

items.meaning: the clearest instance used to anchor a concept
items.meaningCN: 用来锚定概念的最清晰实例
items.example: The paradigm case shapes how other cases are judged.
items.exampleCN: 典型个案决定了其他案例如何被评判。

items.meaning: to treat or present something as a model
items.meaningCN: 把某物当作范式来处理或呈现
items.example: The textbook paradigmatizes one method above the rest.
items.exampleCN: 这本教科书把一种方法树为高于其余的范式。

items.meaning: beside, alongside, beyond
items.example: Parallel, paragraph, paramedic.
items.exampleCN: 平行的、段落、急救员。

items.meaning: to show, to point out
items.example: Deiknynai is the second half of paradeigma.
items.exampleCN: deiknynai 是 paradeigma 的后半部分。

items.meaning: pointing, as in words like this and here
items.meaningCN: 指示性的，如 this、here 这类词
items.example: This and here are deictic words.
items.exampleCN: this 和 here 都是指示词。

latinEntries.structure: Greek paradeigma borrowed into Late Latin
latinEntries.example: Late Latin paradigma passed into Old French and English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁语 paradigma 传入古法语与英语。

latinEntries.example: The Late Latin adjective underlies English paradigmatic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这一晚期拉丁语形容词是英语 paradigmatic 的基础。

definition_zh: 平行的；并列的；类似的；同时进行的；平行线；纬线；类似物；与……相当
definition_en: of two lines or surfaces, always the same distance apart and never meeting; of two things, matching point for point or happening at the same time
core_image: 两条笔直延伸、间距始终不变的轨道，无论走多远都不会相交
scene: 清晨的操场上，两条跑道笔直伸向尽头。The two white lines are parallel: the gap between them stays the same all the way to the far end, and they never meet.
sceneCN: 这里 parallel 是「几何上平行的」（第 1 个义项：间距不变的线）；句意：两条白线是平行的：它们之间的距离一直到尽头都保持不变，永不交汇。图中可辨识物件：红色跑道线、白色分道线、起跑器、远处看台。

pos.zh: 类似的；对应的；可类比的
类似的人或物；可类比之处

forms.label: 过去式／过去分词（美式拼写）
过去式／过去分词（英式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 平行；类似；对应；（修辞）排比
无与伦比的；无可比拟的

senses.title: Never meeting: lines that keep their distance
senses.titleCN: 永不相交：间距不变的线
senses.definition: of two or more lines or surfaces, always the same distance apart and never meeting, even if extended
senses.definitionCN: 指两条或多条线、面之间距离始终相同，即使延长也永不相交
senses.example: The two walls are parallel, so the corridor is the same width throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 两堵墙是平行的，因此走廊从头到尾一样宽。
senses.why: Greek parallēlos is literally 'beside one another': para- 'beside' plus allēlōn 'of each other'. Two lines that run beside each other at a fixed distance never close the gap, and that is the whole image.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 parallēlos 字面就是“彼此并排”：para-“在旁边”加 allēlōn“彼此”。两条线以固定间距并肩延伸，缺口永不闭合，这就是全部画面。

senses.title: Matching point for point
senses.definition: of two things, similar in structure or course so that one can be set against the other
senses.definitionCN: 指两事物在结构或进程上相似，可以一一对照
senses.example: The two countries have parallel histories of industrial growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家有着相似的工业增长历程。
senses.why: If two lines can be laid side by side without either bending, their points can be matched one to one. The geometry becomes a way of saying that two stories run in the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 如果两条线能并排摆放而无需弯折，它们的点就能一一对应。几何于是变成一种说法：两个故事以同一形状展开。

senses.title: Running at the same time
senses.definition: happening or operating at the same time as something else, often independently
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事同时发生或运作，且常常各自独立
senses.example: The two investigations ran in parallel.
senses.exampleCN: 两项调查同时进行。
senses.why: Two tracks laid side by side can carry two runners at once without touching. Time is treated as a track, so parallel work means work that advances beside other work rather than after it.
senses.whyCN: 并排铺好的两条轨道可以同时承载两名跑者而不相碰。时间被当作轨道，于是“并行工作”指与别的工作并肩推进，而不是在其后推进。

senses.title: Parallel circuits and parallel computing
senses.definition: in electricity and computing, arranged so that several paths or processors work at the same time rather than in sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在电学与计算中，安排多条通路或多个处理器同时工作，而非按顺序工作
senses.example: The battery bank is wired in parallel to keep the voltage the same.
senses.exampleCN: 电池组采用并联接线，以保持电压不变。
senses.why: A circuit drawn with branches side by side is a literal parallel: current has several routes that do not merge until the end. Computing borrowed the diagram and the word for processors working side by side.
senses.whyCN: 把支路画成并排的电路图就是字面上的 parallel：电流有多条互不合并的通路，直到末端才汇合。计算领域借用了这张图与这个词，表示并排工作的处理器。

senses.title: A parallel line or plane
senses.definition: a line or plane that is parallel to another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一条线或另一个面平行的线或面
senses.example: Draw a parallel to the base through the apex.
senses.exampleCN: 过顶点作一条与底边平行的线。
senses.why: The adjective names a relation; the noun names one of the two objects standing in that relation. English routinely turns a relation into a countable thing, so a parallel is a line you can draw.
senses.whyCN: 形容词命名一种关系，名词则命名处于该关系中的两个对象之一。英语常把关系变成可数之物，因此 a parallel 就是一条你能画出来的线。

senses.title: Lines on the globe: parallels of latitude
senses.definition: one of the imaginary circles around the earth parallel to the equator
senses.definitionCN: 地球上与赤道平行的假想圆圈之一
senses.example: The ship crossed the fortieth parallel at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船在黎明时越过了北纬四十度线。
senses.why: On a globe, latitude circles never meet and stay equidistant along any meridian. Cartographers therefore called them parallels, and the noun became a way of naming a position north or south.
senses.whyCN: 在地球仪上，纬线圈永不相交，并沿任何经线保持等距。制图者因此称它们为 parallels，这个名词也就成了标记南北位置的方式。

senses.title: A comparison drawn: the parallel between two things
senses.definition: a person, situation, or event that closely resembles another, or the comparison drawn between them
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或事极为相似的人、情形或事件，或由此作出的比较
senses.example: Historians draw a parallel between the two crises.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家在这两场危机之间作类比。
senses.why: To draw a parallel is to lay two cases side by side and show that their outlines match. The noun is the comparison itself, treated as a line you can draw between two points.
senses.whyCN: draw a parallel 就是把两个案例并排摆好，展示它们的轮廓吻合。这个名词就是比较本身，被当作一条能在两点之间画出的线。

senses.title: To parallel: match or run alongside
senses.definition: to be similar or equal to something, or to happen alongside it
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相似或相当，或与其同时发生
senses.example: The rise in rents paralleled the growth in wages.
senses.exampleCN: 租金上涨与工资增长并行发生。
senses.why: The verb keeps the spatial picture: two processes move forward side by side, neither overtaking the other. From that comes both 'to equal' and 'to accompany'.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留空间画面：两个过程并肩前进，谁也不超过谁。由此同时得到“与……相当”和“与……伴随”两层意思。

intro.en: Parallel is Greek in form and Latin in transmission. Its two Greek parts are well documented; the figurative and technical senses grew later in English.
intro.cn: parallel 形出希腊、经由拉丁语传来。两个希腊成分有明确记载；引申义与技术义都是英语后来长出来的。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English, meaning 'of lines that never meet'. It comes from Latin parallelus, from Greek parallēlos.
items.cn: 形容词最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，意为“永不相交的线”。它来自拉丁语 parallelus，再上溯希腊语 parallēlos。

items.en: Parallēlos is formed from para- 'beside' and allēlōn 'of one another', the reciprocal form of allos 'other'. The compound says that the two things stand beside each other.
items.cn: parallēlos 由 para-“在旁边”与 allēlōn“彼此”构成，后者是 allos“另一个”的相互形式。这个复合词说的就是“两物彼此并立”。

items.en: Allos 'other' goes back to PIE *al- 'beyond, other', the source also of English else and alien. The asterisk marks a reconstructed root.
items.cn: allos“另一个”上溯原始印欧语 *al-“超出、另外”，也是英语 else 与 alien 的来源。星号表示重构词根。

items.en: The noun appears, meaning 'a parallel line'. By the 1590s the word is used for a comparison, and the verb follows with the sense 'to place side by side'.
items.cn: 名词于 16 世纪 50 年代出现，意为“平行线”。到 16 世纪 90 年代，词义扩展到“类比”，动词随后出现，意为“并排摆放”。

items.en: Technology gives the word new weight: parallel circuit, parallel processing, massively parallel computers, and the popular parallel universe. The diagram of side-by-side paths is still doing the work.
items.cn: 技术赋予这个词新的分量：并联电路、并行处理、大规模并行计算机，以及流行的“平行宇宙”。并排通路的图示仍在承担表义工作。

note.en: The first group is other para- words that look close; the second compares words for similarity and coexistence.
note.cn: 第一组是其他形近的 para- 词；第二组比较表示“相似与共存”的词。

entries.definition: the apparent shift in an object's position when the observer moves. Its second part is allassein 'to change', not allēlōn.
entries.definitionCN: 观察者移动时物体位置的视位移。它的后半是 allassein“改变”，不是 allēlōn。

entries.definition: a section of writing. The second part is graphein 'to write'; the para- is also 'beside'.
entries.definitionCN: 文章的一个段落。后半是 graphein“写”；para- 同样是“在旁边”。

entries.definition: loss of movement or function. Its second part is lysis 'a loosening', and the para- means beside or beyond.
entries.definitionCN: 失去运动或功能。后半是 lysis“松开”，para- 意为“在旁边、超出”。

entries.definition: more important than anything else. It comes from par 'equal' plus amont 'above', not from para- plus allos.
entries.definitionCN: 高于一切的。它来自 par“同等”加 amont“在上”，不是 para- 加 allos。

entries.definition: similar in function or structure though not in origin. It stresses a usable comparison, while parallel stresses matching course or shape.
entries.definitionCN: 功能或结构上相似，尽管来源不同。它强调可用的类比，parallel 强调进程或形状的一致。

entries.definition: matching or related one to one. It is the plain adjective for a pairing; parallel adds the image of two lines running together.
entries.definitionCN: 一一对应或相关的。它是表示配对的最朴素形容词；parallel 则加上“两条线并行”的画面。

entries.definition: happening at exactly the same time. It is purely temporal, while parallel can also mean structurally similar.
entries.definitionCN: 恰在同一时间发生。它纯粹指时间，而 parallel 还可指结构相似。

entries.definition: similar enough to be compared fairly. It is about the legitimacy of comparison, not about the shape of the two things.
entries.definitionCN: 相似到可以公平比较的。它说的是比较是否成立，而不是两者形状是否一致。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the rails and the para- prefix, then three abstract images about lines that never meet.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕“轨道”与 para- 前缀的挂钩，再用三个关于“永不相交的线”的抽象画面。

normal.en: Railway tracks are the picture: two steel lines, one distance, no meeting point. That is parallel.
normal.cn: 铁轨就是画面：两条钢线，一个间距，没有交点。这就是 parallel。

normal.en: para- means beside, and -allel comes from allos 'other': two others standing beside each other.
normal.cn: para- 是“在旁边”，-allel 来自 allos“另一个”：两个“另一个”彼此并立。

normal.en: In parallel means side by side in time: two jobs running at once, like two trains on two tracks.
normal.cn: in parallel 指时间上并排：两项工作同时跑，像两列火车在两条轨道上。

normal.en: Parallel bars in gymnastics are two bars at the same height; the name is the geometry.
normal.cn: 体操的 parallel bars 是两根等高的横杆；名字本身就是几何。

normal.en: Spell it with one l in the middle and two at the end of the British verb: parallel, parallelled. The double l marks the British style.
normal.cn: 拼写注意：中间一个 l，英式动词过去式末尾双 l：parallel、parallelled。双 l 是英式标志。

abstract.en: Parallel lines are a promise of distance: they can be as close as you like and still never touch.
abstract.cn: 平行线是一种距离的承诺：可以无限接近，却始终不接触。

abstract.en: To call two histories parallel is to claim that different lives obeyed the same geometry.
abstract.cn: 把两段历史称为 parallel，就是在断言不同的生活服从同一套几何。

abstract.en: Parallel work multiplies capacity but not time: more tracks do not make the train arrive earlier.
abstract.cn: 并行工作增加的是容量，不是时间：轨道再多，也不会让这列火车更早到。

examples.en: The road runs parallel to the river for nearly ten miles.
examples.cn: 这条路与河平行延伸近十英里。

examples.en: The minister drew a parallel between the current shortages and the crisis of 1973.
examples.cn: 部长把当前的短缺与 1973 年的危机作了类比。

examples.en: The software divides the image into blocks and processes them in parallel.
examples.cn: 该软件把图像分成区块并并行处理。

dict_mnemonic.note: para- 记成“在旁边”，allel 记成“彼此”：两样东西彼此并排、间距不变，就是平行。
dict_mnemonic.text: para（在旁边）+ allēlōn（彼此）→ 彼此并排 → 平行的、类似物、类比

root: 希腊 parallēlos“彼此并排”，para（在旁边）+ allēlōn（彼此；allos“另一个”，原始印欧语 *al-）→ 拉丁 parallelus → 英语 parallel。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow the geometry outward: two lines that never meet, two things that match point for point, two processes that run at once, paths in a circuit or a computer, a drawn line, a latitude circle, a comparison, and finally a verb for matching or accompanying.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项沿着几何向外扩展：永不相交的两条线，逐点对应的两件事，同时推进的两个过程，电路或计算机中的多条通路，一条画出的平行线，一条纬线圈，一次类比，最后是表示“相当或伴随”的动词。

core.en: Two rails held at a fixed distance, running on without ever touching
core.cn: 两条保持固定间距、一直延伸却始终不接触的轨道

branches.en: The relation: lines that keep their distance and never meet.
branches.cn: 关系：保持间距、永不相交的线。

branches.en: Resemblance: structures that match, and the comparison you draw between them.
branches.cn: 相似：彼此吻合的结构，以及你在它们之间画出的比较。

branches.en: Coexistence: processes running side by side, whether in time or in a circuit.
branches.cn: 共存：并排推进的过程，无论是在时间上还是在电路里。

branches.en: Drawn lines at every scale: a line on paper and a circle around the globe.
branches.cn: 各个尺度上的线：纸上的一条线，与绕地球一圈的纬线。

branches.en: The verb: to match something, or to run alongside it.
branches.cn: 动词：与某物相当，或与它并肩而行。

intro.en: Parallel's family is built on the Greek pair para- and allos. The derivatives below are mostly modern technical formations, plus one negated adjective that is older and figurative.
intro.cn: parallel 的词族建立在希腊语的 para- 与 allos 这一对成分上。下面的派生词多为现代技术造词，另有一个更早、更引申的否定形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin parallelus is a borrowing of Greek parallēlos, and Medieval Latin parallelismus gave English parallelism. Latin adds no new element; it transmits the Greek compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 parallelus 是希腊语 parallēlos 的借用，中世纪拉丁语 parallelismus 则给出英语 parallelism。拉丁语没有增加新成分，只是转送这个希腊复合词。

items.meaning: never meeting; matching; simultaneous
items.meaningCN: 永不相交；相对应；同时的
items.example: The two paths are parallel.
items.exampleCN: 这两条小路是平行的。

items.meaning: a parallel line, a latitude circle, or a comparison
items.example: The 38th parallel divides the peninsula.
items.exampleCN: 三十八度线把半岛分开。

items.meaning: to equal, match, or run alongside
items.example: Nothing parallels that season of growth.
items.exampleCN: 没有哪个时期能比得上那个增长季。

items.meaning: the state of being parallel; a matching of structures; rhetorical balance
items.meaningCN: 平行状态；结构对应；修辞上的排比
items.example: The poem uses parallelism in every stanza.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗每一节都用了排比。

items.meaning: to arrange work so that parts run at the same time
items.meaningCN: 使并行；把工作安排成同时执行
items.example: The compiler parallelizes the loop.
items.exampleCN: 编译器把这个循环并行化。

items.meaning: the process of making tasks run in parallel
items.example: Parallelization cut the run time by half.
items.exampleCN: 并行化把运行时间缩短了一半。

items.meaning: having no equal; unmatched
items.meaningCN: 无与伦比的；无可比拟的
items.example: The response was unparalleled in speed.
items.exampleCN: 这一反应的迅速程度无与伦比。

items.meaning: not parallel; not corresponding
items.example: Nonparallel walls distort the room.
items.exampleCN: 不平行的墙面让房间变形。

items.meaning: goods imported through unofficial channels alongside authorized ones
items.meaningCN: 与授权渠道并行的非官方进口货（平行进口）
items.example: Parallel imports undercut the official price.
items.exampleCN: 平行进口压低了官方价格。

latinEntries.example: Latin parallelus is the direct source of the English adjective.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 parallelus 是英语形容词的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin parallelismus underlies English parallelism.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 parallelismus 是英语 parallelism 的基础。

definition_zh: 参数；参量；（可调的）指标；界限；限定因素
definition_en: a measurable quantity that defines a system or model and can be set or varied; also a limit that bounds what is possible
core_image: 一块写满公式的白板旁边，立着几根可调的刻度尺，每一根都决定曲线往哪边弯
scene: 实验室的白板上写着一个模型公式，旁边列着三个可调旋钮。Each knob is a parameter of the model, and turning it changes the shape of the whole curve.
sceneCN: 这里 parameter 是「模型中的可调参量」（第 1 个义项：决定模型形状的量）；句意：每个旋钮都是模型的一个参数，拧动它就会改变整条曲线的形状。图中可辨识物件：白板公式、三个旋钮、刻度盘、曲线图、记号笔。

senses.title: A value that shapes a model
senses.definition: in mathematics, a quantity that is fixed for one case but can vary between cases, and whose value determines the form of an equation or curve
senses.definitionCN: 数学中在单个情形里固定、但可在不同情形间变化的量，其取值决定方程或曲线的形态
senses.example: Changing the parameter a turns the circle into an ellipse.
senses.exampleCN: 改变参数 a，圆就变成了椭圆。
senses.why: Greek para- means beside and metron means measure: a parameter is a measure set beside the main variables. It does not move during one calculation, yet it decides the shape of the whole result.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 para- 是“在旁边”，metron 是“度量”：参数就是摆在主要变量旁边的一把尺。它在一次计算中不动，却决定整个结果的形状。

senses.title: The population parameter in statistics
senses.definition: in statistics, a true numerical characteristic of a whole population, usually unknown and estimated from a sample
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中整个总体的真实数值特征，通常未知，需由样本估计
senses.example: The population mean is a parameter, while the sample mean is a statistic.
senses.exampleCN: 总体均值是参数，样本均值是统计量。
senses.why: Statistics splits the unseen whole from the visible part. The parameter belongs to the whole and is therefore fixed but unknown; the statistic belongs to the sample and is calculated. The word keeps its sense of a measure that stands beside the data.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把看不见的总体与看得见的部分分开。参数属于总体，因而固定却未知；统计量属于样本，是被算出来的。这个词仍保留“摆在数据旁边的度量”之意。

senses.title: An argument passed to a function
senses.definition: in computing, a value supplied to a function, routine, or command that changes what it does
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中传给函数、例程或命令的值，用以改变其行为
senses.example: The function takes two parameters: a file name and a size.
senses.exampleCN: 这个函数接收两个参数：文件名和大小。
senses.why: A function is a small machine with settings. The values you hand it are measures set beside the operation, deciding which case it handles; programming simply inherited the mathematical word.
senses.whyCN: 函数是一台带设定的小机器。你交给它的值就是摆在操作旁边的度量，决定它处理哪一种情形；编程只是继承了数学里的这个词。

senses.title: A design or operating parameter
senses.definition: in engineering and design, a measurable specification that a product or process must meet
senses.definitionCN: 工程与设计中产品或过程必须满足的可测规格
senses.example: The bridge was built to withstand wind parameters far above the legal minimum.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥按远高于法定最低值的风力参数建造。
senses.why: An engineer cannot test every future wind. Instead the design is fixed to numbers that stand for the conditions, and those numbers are the parameters. The measure now controls the object rather than describing it.
senses.whyCN: 工程师无法测试未来每一种风。于是把设计固定在代表这些条件的数字上，这些数字就是参数。度量在这里不是描述对象，而是控制对象。

senses.title: The limits within which you may act
senses.definition: usually in the plural, the limits or boundaries that define what is possible or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 通常用复数，指界定何为可能或可接受的界限
senses.example: We must work within the parameters of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须在预算范围内工作。
senses.why: A parameter fixes a value, and a set of fixed values marks out a space of allowed cases. English speakers turned that space into a boundary, so working within parameters means staying inside the range the numbers permit.
senses.whyCN: 一个参数固定一个值，一组固定值就划出一片允许的情形空间。英语使用者把这片空间理解为边界，因此“在参数之内工作”就是待在这些数字允许的范围内。

senses.title: A limiting factor
senses.definition: a factor that limits or determines the character of a situation or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 限制或决定某一情形、结果性质的因素
senses.example: Cost is the main parameter of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是这个项目的主要限定因素。
senses.why: This sense pushes the word from a number to a factor that behaves like a number: it sets the conditions others must fit. Some usage guides object that limit would be clearer, but the extension follows the same logic of a value that governs a range.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把词从“一个数字”推到“像数字那样起作用的因素”：它设定别人必须迁就的条件。有些用法指南认为用 limit 更清楚，但这一扩展仍沿着“一个值支配一片范围”的逻辑。

senses.title: A measured physical quantity
senses.definition: in science, a measurable quantity such as temperature or pressure that characterizes a system
senses.definitionCN: 科学中表征系统的可测量，如温度或压力
senses.example: Temperature and salinity are the key parameters of the seawater model.
senses.exampleCN: 温度和盐度是海水模型的关键参数。
senses.why: Here the word comes close to its Greek parts again: a measure taken beside the system, entered into the model. The quantity is not the system itself but a number that stands for one aspect of it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词又贴近了它的希腊成分：在系统旁边取得的一个度量，被输入模型。这个量不是系统本身，而是代表系统某一侧面的数字。

senses.title: A switch in universal grammar
senses.titleCN: 普遍语法中的一个参数
senses.definition: in linguistics, one of a small set of grammatical options that a language fixes, such as whether it drops subjects
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中一门语言所固定的少数语法选项之一，如是否允许省略主语
senses.example: The pro-drop parameter distinguishes Spanish from English.
senses.exampleCN: 省略主语参数把西班牙语与英语区分开来。
senses.why: In Chomskyan theory the universal grammar is a system with a few switches, and each switch is a parameter. The metaphor is exact: a small setting beside the main system, fixed to one value, which explains a whole family of surface differences.
senses.whyCN: 在乔姆斯基的理论里，普遍语法是一套带几个开关的系统，每个开关就是一个参数。这个比喻很精确：主系统旁边的一个小设定，固定为某个值，就能解释一整族表层差异。

intro.en: Parameter is a scientific coinage from two Greek parts. Its mathematical sense is old; the statistical, computing, and 'limits' senses are modern, and the last one is often criticised as an extension.
intro.cn: parameter 是由两个希腊成分构成的科学造词。其数学义较老；统计、计算与“界限”三义都是现代新增，最后一义常被批评为扩展过度。

items.en: Parameter appears in geometry, in the treatment of conic sections, meaning a fixed line or length used to describe a curve. It is formed in Modern Latin from Greek parts.
items.cn: parameter 于 17 世纪 50 年代出现在几何学中，用于讨论圆锥曲线，指描述曲线时使用的一条定线或定长。它是在近代拉丁语中用希腊成分构成的。

items.en: The parts are para- 'beside, subsidiary' and metron 'measure'. Metron goes back to PIE *me- 'to measure', the same family as meter, metre, and measure.
items.cn: 两个成分是 para-“在旁边、辅助”与 metron“度量”。metron 上溯原始印欧语 *me-“测量”，与 meter、metre、measure 同族。

items.en: The word spreads through mathematics as the general name for a quantity that is constant within a problem but can be varied between problems.
items.cn: 这个词在数学中扩散开来，泛指在单个问题内保持不变、但在不同问题之间可以变化的量。

items.en: Statistics adopts the term for a true characteristic of a population, as opposed to a statistic computed from a sample. The distinction becomes standard in sampling theory.
items.cn: 统计学采用这个术语，指总体的真实特征，与由样本算出的统计量相对。这一区分在抽样理论中成为标准。

items.en: The 'limits' sense spreads in general usage, probably helped by the sound of perimeter. Usage guides often call it imprecise, since a parameter is a value rather than a boundary, but the sense is now widespread in business and policy writing.
items.cn: “界限”义在一般用法中扩散，可能受到 perimeter 读音的影响。用法指南常说它不精确，因为参数是取值而不是边界；但在商业与政策写作中，这一义项如今已很常见。

note.en: The first group is the -meter family, which shares metron but differs in prefix; the second compares words for values, factors, and limits.
note.cn: 第一组是 -meter 词族，共享 metron 但前缀不同；第二组比较表示“取值、因素与界限”的词。

entries.definition: the distance around a closed shape. Its prefix is peri- 'around', and its sound has probably influenced the 'limits' sense of parameter.
entries.definitionCN: 封闭图形一周的长度。其前缀是 peri-“环绕”，它的读音很可能影响了 parameter 的“界限”义。

entries.definition: an instrument that measures air pressure. The second element is the same metron, the first is baros 'weight'.
entries.definitionCN: 测量气压的仪器。后半是同一个 metron，前半是 baros“重量”。

entries.definition: a straight line through the centre of a circle. Its dia- means across, so it is a measure across, not beside.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过圆心的直线。它的 dia- 意为“穿过”，所以是“横量”，而不是“旁量”。

entries.definition: an instrument for measuring temperature. Same metron, different prefix: heat
entries.definitionCN: 测量温度的仪器。同一个 metron，不同前缀：热。

entries.definition: a quantity that can change within a problem. A parameter is held fixed within one case, which is the standard contrast in modelling.
entries.definitionCN: 在一个问题内可以变化的量。参数在单个情形里保持固定，这是建模中的标准对照。

entries.definition: one of the elements that contributes to a result. It is causal and often qualitative, while parameter is measurable and settable.
entries.definitionCN: 促成结果的要素之一。它偏因果、常为定性，而 parameter 可测量、可设定。

entries.definition: the point beyond which something stops. It is the plain word for a boundary and is often recommended over parameter in the 'limits' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物停止的那条线。它是表示边界的最普通词，在“界限”义上常被建议用来替代 parameter。

entries.definition: a detailed requirement that a product must meet. It is a stated requirement, while a parameter is a quantity used to define or control the system.
entries.definitionCN: 产品必须满足的详细要求。它是被写明的规格，而 parameter 是用来定义或控制系统的一个量。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the two Greek parts, then three abstract images about settings that govern a range.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕两个希腊成分的挂钩，再用三个关于“设定支配范围”的抽象画面。

normal.en: para- beside, meter measure: a parameter is a measuring stick standing beside the equation.
normal.cn: para- 在旁边，meter 度量：参数就是立在方程旁边的一把量尺。

normal.en: Picture a sound desk: each slider is a parameter. Move one, and the whole sound changes.
normal.cn: 想象一张调音台：每个推子就是一个参数。推动一个，整个声音都变。

normal.en: A function call like draw(x, y, size) passes parameters; the brackets are where the settings go.
normal.cn: 像 draw(x, y, size) 这样的函数调用传的就是参数；括号就是放设定的地方。

normal.en: Statisticians pair them: parameter belongs to the population, statistic belongs to the sample. Whole versus part.
normal.cn: 统计学家把它们配对：参数属于总体，统计量属于样本。整体对部分。

normal.en: Beware perimeter: it sounds like parameter and means the line around a shape. Around is not beside.
normal.cn: 当心 perimeter：读音像 parameter，意思却是图形一周的线。around 不是 beside。

abstract.en: A parameter is a small decision that decides a large shape: one number fixed in advance, and a whole family of curves follows.
abstract.cn: 参数是一个决定大形状的小决定：一个数字事先定好，一整族曲线随之而来。

abstract.en: Parameters are the handles a system gives you. What you cannot reach is not a parameter but a constraint.
abstract.cn: 参数是系统交给你的把手。你够不到的东西不是参数，而是约束。

abstract.en: Naming a limit a parameter flatters it: it makes a wall sound like a dial.
abstract.cn: 把界限叫作参数是在给它贴金：让一堵墙听起来像一个旋钮。

examples.en: The model has three parameters, and each must be estimated from the data.
examples.cn: 这个模型有三个参数，每一个都必须由数据估计。

examples.en: You can adjust the display parameters in the settings menu.
examples.cn: 你可以在设置菜单里调整显示参数。

examples.en: The committee has to decide whether the plan falls within the parameters of the grant.
examples.cn: 委员会必须判断该计划是否落在资助范围内。

dict_mnemonic.note: para- 记成“在旁边”，meter 记成“量”：摆在主变量旁边、用来定形状的那个量，就是参数。
dict_mnemonic.text: para（在旁边）+ metron（度量）→ 旁边的量度 → 参数、参量；被引申为“界限”

root: 希腊 para-（在旁边、辅助）+ metron（度量，原始印欧语 *me-）→ 近代拉丁 parameter → 英语 parameter。

sensesIntro.en: The senses begin with a value set beside an equation, move to the unseen value of a population, to the value handed to a function, to the number a design must meet, then to the range those numbers allow, to a limiting factor, to a measured physical quantity, and finally to a switch in universal grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“摆在方程旁边的取值”开始，转到总体的未知值、传给函数的值、设计必须满足的数字，再由这些数字划出的范围，转到限定因素、可测物理量，最后落到普遍语法里的一个开关。

core.en: A row of adjustable scales standing beside one equation, each bending the curve
core.cn: 立在一条方程旁边的一排可调刻度，每一格都让曲线换形

branches.en: The model and the whole: a value that shapes an equation, and the true value of a population.
branches.cn: 模型与总体：决定方程形状的取值，以及总体的真实值。

branches.en: Inputs to systems: a value passed to a function, and a physical quantity fed into a model.
branches.cn: 系统的输入：传给函数的值，以及输入模型的物理量。

branches.en: Specification: the measurable numbers a design must meet.
branches.cn: 规格：一项设计必须满足的、可测量的数字。

branches.en: The disputed extension: a boundary treated as a factor, and a factor treated as a setting.
branches.cn: 有争议的扩展：把边界当作因素，又把因素当作设定。

branches.en: A switch in universal grammar: one of the few options a language fixes.
branches.cn: 普遍语法中的一个开关：一门语言所固定的少数选项之一。

intro.en: Parameter's family is technical and regular: the adjective, the adverb, the verb of setting parameters, and the participle. The prefix para- and the root metron are shared with a large measuring family.
intro.cn: parameter 的词族技术性强而规则：形容词、副词、表示“设定参数”的动词及其分词。前缀 para- 与词根 metron 与一个庞大的“测量”词族共享。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin parameter was coined from Greek parts, and Latin metrum (from Greek metron) is the source of English metre and meter. The Greek compound, not a Latin root, is the true origin.
latinIntro.cn: 近代拉丁语 parameter 是用希腊成分新造的；拉丁语 metrum（来自希腊语 metron）则是英语 metre 与 meter 的来源。真正的源头是希腊复合词，而不是拉丁词根。

items.meaning: a fixed or settable quantity that defines a system
items.meaningCN: 定义系统的固定或可设定量
items.example: The parameter controls the slope of the line.
items.exampleCN: 这个参数控制直线的斜率。

items.meaning: expressed by or relating to parameters
items.example: The software builds parametric models.
items.exampleCN: 该软件构建参数化模型。

items.meaning: in terms of parameters
items.example: The curve is defined parametrically.
items.exampleCN: 这条曲线是用参数方式定义的。

items.meaning: to express or control something by parameters
items.meaningCN: 参数化；用参数表示或控制
items.example: They parameterized the model by grain size.
items.exampleCN: 他们按颗粒大小对模型进行参数化。

items.meaning: the act or result of expressing something in parameters
items.example: A good parameterization reduces the error.
items.exampleCN: 良好的参数化能降低误差。

items.meaning: set up so that values can be supplied
items.meaningCN: 已参数化的；可传入取值的
items.example: The parameterized query avoids injection.
items.exampleCN: 参数化查询可避免注入攻击。

items.meaning: beside, alongside, subsidiary
items.example: Parallel, paramedic, parameter.
items.exampleCN: 平行的、急救员、参数。

items.meaning: measure, a measured length
items.example: Metron is the second half of parameter.
items.exampleCN: metron 是 parameter 的后半部分。

items.meaning: the measured line around a shape
items.meaningCN: 绕图形一周量出的线；周长
items.example: The perimeter of the square is four times one side.
items.exampleCN: 正方形的周长是一边长的四倍。

latinEntries.structure: Modern Latin coinage from Greek parts
latinEntries.meaning: a line or measure used to describe a curve
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用来描述曲线的一条定线或度量
latinEntries.example: Parameter entered English from the Latin of geometry.
latinEntries.exampleCN: parameter 经几何学的拉丁语进入英语。

latinEntries.example: Latin metrum gave English metre.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 metrum 给出英语 metre。

definition_zh: 参与；参加；分享（收益、成本）；持有份额；（古旧）具有某种性质
definition_en: to take part in an activity or share in something with others; in older usage, to have a quality in common with something
core_image: 一只手伸进共同的事务里，并从中分到属于自己的一份
scene: 社区花园里，居民卷起袖子一起翻土、分种子、抬水桶。Everyone who came to the garden was asked to participate, and at the end each helper took home a basket of vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 participate 是「参与活动」（第 1 个义项：参加一项活动）；句意：每个来花园的人都被邀请参与，最后每位帮手都带回家一篮蔬菜。图中可辨识物件：铁锹、种子袋、水桶、菜畦、收成篮。

pos.zh: （古旧、正式）具有；带有（某种性质）

derivatives.zh: 参与性的（多指管理风格）
不参与的；不参加分红的

senses.title: Take part in an activity
senses.definition: to take part in an event, activity, or process with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起参加某项事件、活动或过程
senses.example: More than fifty students participated in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 五十多名学生参加了这项调查。
senses.why: Latin particeps means 'taking a part', from pars 'part' plus capere 'to take'. To participate is literally to take a part for oneself in something larger, which is why the verb always needs a whole to enter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 particeps 意为“拿取一份”，由 pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”构成。participate 字面就是“在一个更大的事情里为自己拿一份”，因此这个动词总需要一个可进入的整体。

senses.title: Take part actively: put yourself in
senses.definition: to involve oneself actively rather than merely being present
senses.definitionCN: 主动投入，而不只是身在现场
senses.example: She participated eagerly in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她热切地参与了辩论。
senses.why: Taking a part is an action, not a seat. The word therefore implies effort: the participant reaches into the activity, while a spectator only watches it.
senses.whyCN: “拿一份”是动作，不是占个座位。因此这个词隐含付出：参与者把手伸进活动中，而旁观者只是看着。

senses.title: Share in the results
senses.definition: to share in profits, costs, or benefits with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人分享利润、成本或收益
senses.example: The workers participate in the profits of the cooperative.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们分享合作社的利润。
senses.why: The 'part' taken can be a share of the outcome rather than a role in the work. English extends the word from joining an activity to receiving a portion of what the activity produces.
senses.whyCN: 所拿的“一份”可以是成果中的份额，而不只是工作中的一个角色。英语把这个词从“加入活动”扩展到“分得活动产出的一部分”。

senses.title: Hold a share: participating policies
senses.definition: in finance and insurance, to have a right to a share of profits or assets
senses.definitionCN: 在金融与保险中，拥有分得利润或资产的权利
senses.example: The policy is participating, so it receives annual dividends.
senses.exampleCN: 这是分红型保单，因此每年获得红利。
senses.why: Once a share can be owned, participation becomes a property right written into a contract. The word moves from doing to holding, but the underlying image is still a portion set aside for the holder.
senses.whyCN: 当“一份”可以被拥有，参与就变成写进合同的财产权。这个词从“做事”转到“持有”，但底层画面仍是为持有者留出的那一份。

senses.title: Take part in decisions
senses.definition: to have a voice or a role in making decisions that affect a group
senses.definitionCN: 在影响群体的决策中有发言权或一份作用
senses.example: Employees participate in decisions about working hours.
senses.exampleCN: 员工参与有关工时的决策。
senses.why: Decision-making is an activity with roles inside it. To participate is to hold one of those roles, which is why the word appears in arguments about democracy and workplace governance.
senses.whyCN: 决策是一项内部有角色的活动。参与就是持有其中一个角色，因此这个词会出现在关于民主与工作场所治理的讨论中。

senses.title: Enter a competition
senses.definition: to compete or take part in a contest, tournament, or exhibition
senses.definitionCN: 参加比赛、锦标赛或展览
senses.example: Twelve teams participated in the tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 十二支队伍参加了锦标赛。
senses.why: A contest is a structured whole with a fixed number of places. Entering it is taking one of those places, so the verb fits competitions as naturally as meetings.
senses.whyCN: 比赛是一个结构化的整体，名额固定。报名参赛就是占其中一个位置，因此这个动词用于竞赛和用于会议一样自然。

senses.title: Enrol as a research subject
senses.definition: to enrol oneself as a subject in a clinical trial or research study
senses.definitionCN: 作为受试者加入临床试验或研究
senses.example: Two hundred patients participated in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 两百名患者参加了这项试验。
senses.why: In a trial the participant contributes data rather than labour. The word still means taking a part, but the part is now a measured role inside a protocol, and ethics rules grow around it.
senses.whyCN: 在试验中，参与者贡献的是数据而不是劳动。这个词仍表示“拿一份”，但这一份现在是研究方案里被测量的角色，伦理规范也随之围绕它生长。

senses.title: Have a quality in common (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 具有某种性质（古旧用法）
senses.definition: in older usage with of, to have a quality or nature in common with something
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，与 of 连用，表示与某物共有某种性质或本性
senses.example: The essay participates of the nature of a confession.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章带有自白的性质。
senses.why: In scholastic language, sharing a quality was treated as having a share in a form. The construction participate of is a fossil of that metaphysics, which is why it now sounds literary and old.
senses.whyCN: 在经院哲学语言里，“共有一项性质”被理解为“分有一个形式”。participate of 这一结构就是那套形而上学的化石，因此今天听来既文学又古旧。

intro.en: Participate is a Latin verb built from 'part' and 'take'. Its English life began as a back-formation, and the two halves are well documented.
intro.cn: participate 是一个由“部分”与“拿取”构成的拉丁动词。它在英语中的生命始于逆构，两个成分都有明确记载。

items.en: The English verb is recorded, probably a back-formation from participation or taken directly from Latin participatus, the past participle of participare.
items.cn: 英语动词记录于 16 世纪 30 年代，很可能是从 participation 逆构而来，或直接取自拉丁语 participare 的过去分词 participatus。

items.en: Participare 'to share, take part' comes from particeps 'sharing, taking part'. Particeps joins pars 'part' with the -cip- element of capere 'to take, seize'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 participare“分享、参加”来自 particeps“分享的、参加的”。particeps 把 pars“部分”与 capere“拿取、抓住”的 -cip- 成分结合起来。

items.en: Pars goes back to PIE *pere- 'to grant, allot', the family of portion and parcel. Capere goes back to *kap- 'to grasp', the family of capture and accept. The asterisks mark reconstructed roots.
items.cn: pars 上溯原始印欧语 *pere-“给予、分配”，是 portion 与 parcel 的词族。capere 上溯 *kap-“抓取”，是 capture 与 accept 的词族。星号表示重构词根。

items.en: The construction participate of appears, meaning 'to have a quality in common with'. It belongs to scholastic talk of sharing in a form and is now archaic.
items.cn: participate of 这一结构出现于 16 世纪 60 年代，意为“与……共有某种性质”。它属于经院哲学关于“分有形式”的说法，如今已属古旧。

items.en: Finance and insurance extend the word to profit-sharing: participating policy, participating shares. Twentieth-century institutions add participatory democracy and clinical trial participation.
items.cn: 金融与保险把词扩展到利润分享：分红型保单、参与分红的股份。20 世纪的制度又添上“参与式民主”与“临床试验参与”。

note.en: The first group is built on the same part- root but means something else; the second compares verbs of joining.
note.cn: 第一组同样带 part- 词根但意思不同；第二组比较表示“加入”的动词。

entries.definition: a verb form used as an adjective, such as broken or running. It comes from Latin participium 'a sharing', so it is a relative of participate but not a form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用作形容词的动词形式，如 broken 或 running。它来自拉丁语 participium“分享”，因而是 participate 的亲戚，却不是它的词形变化。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. It is the noun from participate, not a separate verb.
entries.definitionCN: 参与者。它是 participate 派生的名词，不是另一个动词。

entries.definition: the act of taking part. The -ion suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的行为。-ion 后缀把动词变成动作名词。

entries.definition: concerning only a part; biased. It shares the pars root but has no capere element and does not mean taking part.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的；偏袒的。它共享 pars 词根，但没有 capere 成分，也不表示“参加”。

entries.definition: to be present at an event. It stresses presence, while participate stresses contributing or sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 出席某个活动。它强调在场，而 participate 强调贡献或分享。

entries.definition: to become a member of a group or activity. It marks entry, while participate marks the activity once inside.
entries.definitionCN: 成为某群体或活动的一员。它标记“进入”，而 participate 标记进入之后的活动。

entries.definition: to become involved with something, often with commitment. It is broader and can be passive or hostile as well as cooperative.
entries.definitionCN: 投入某事，常含承诺。它更宽泛，既可合作，也可被动甚至对抗。

entries.definition: to give something such as effort, money, or ideas to a shared purpose. It stresses what is given, while participate stresses being one of the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标付出努力、金钱或想法。它强调“给出什么”，而 participate 强调“成为其中一份”。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on part + take, then three abstract images about shares and belonging.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 part + take 的挂钩，再用三个关于“份额与归属”的抽象画面。

normal.en: Split it: parti- is part, -cip- is take (as in capture). Participate = take a part.
normal.cn: 拆开看：parti- 是“部分”，-cip- 是“拿取”（如 capture）。participate＝拿一份。

normal.en: participate in, not participate at: you enter a whole, so the preposition is in.
normal.cn: 是 participate in，不是 participate at：你进入的是一个整体，所以介词用 in。

normal.en: A participant is one who took a part; the -ant ending marks the person holding the share.
normal.cn: participant 就是“拿了那一份的人”；-ant 结尾标记持有这份的人。

normal.en: In a meeting, presence is attendance; speaking is participation. Two different words for two different levels.
normal.cn: 在会上，到场是 attendance，发言才是 participation。两个词对应两个层次。

normal.en: A participating policy pays you a part of the profits; the same 'share' idea, now in money.
normal.cn: 分红型保单（participating policy）把一部分利润分给你；还是“一份”的意思，只是换成了钱。

abstract.en: To participate is to accept a share of both the work and the consequence; the two cannot be separated.
abstract.cn: 参与就是同时接受工作与后果中的一份；这两者无法分开。

abstract.en: A whole is made of parts that agreed to be counted. Participation is the act of being counted.
abstract.cn: 整体由同意被计入的部分组成。参与就是让自己被计入的动作。

abstract.en: The older sense reminds us that things can share a nature, not only a task: participation began as metaphysics before it became management.
abstract.cn: 古旧义提醒我们：事物不仅能共担任务，也能共有本性——参与先是一种形而上学，然后才成为管理术语。

examples.en: All staff are encouraged to participate in the safety review.
examples.cn: 鼓励全体员工参与安全审查。

examples.en: The company participates in a pension scheme for every employee.
examples.cn: 公司为每位员工参加了一项养老金计划。

examples.en: She participated of a stubbornness that ran in the family.
examples.cn: 她身上带有这个家族遗传的固执。

dict_mnemonic.note: parti- 记成“部分”，-cip- 记成“拿”（capere）：伸手拿一份，就是参与。
dict_mnemonic.text: parti（部分）+ cip（拿取）+ -ate（动词）→ 拿一份 → 参与、分享

root: 拉丁 particeps“分享的、参与的”＝pars“部分”（原始印欧语 *pere-“分配”）+ -cip-（capere“拿取”，*kap-）→ participare → participate。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from taking a part in an activity, to taking it actively, to sharing the results, holding a financial share, joining decisions, entering a contest, enrolling in a trial, and finally the old metaphysical sense of sharing a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“在活动中拿一份”开始，转到积极投入、分享成果、持有金融份额、参与决策、报名参赛、加入试验，最后落到古旧的形而上学义：共有一项性质。

core.en: A hand reaching into a shared task and coming away with its own portion
core.cn: 一只手伸进共同的事务，并从中取走属于自己的那一份

chain: HAVE A SHARE OF A QUALITY

branches.en: Entering structured wholes: an activity, a survey, or a tournament with limited places.
branches.cn: 进入结构化的整体：活动、调查，或名额有限的比赛。

branches.en: From effort to voice: active involvement, and a role in deciding.
branches.cn: 从出力到发声：积极投入，以及在决策中的一份角色。

branches.en: The share as income: profit-sharing, and a contractual right to dividends.
branches.cn: 作为收入的份额：分享利润，以及合同上的分红权。

branches.en: The measured role: a trial subject is still taking part, but inside a protocol.
branches.cn: 被测量的角色：受试者仍在“参加”，只是身处研究方案之中。

branches.en: The old sense: to have a quality in common with something, used with of.
branches.cn: 古旧义：与某物共有某种性质，常与 of 连用。

intro.en: Participate belongs to the part- family and the capere family. The derivatives below show the person, the act, the adjective of style, and the financial participle.
intro.cn: participate 属于 part- 词族，也属于 capere 词族。下面的派生词展示了人、行为、风格形容词，以及金融用法中的分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin participare and particeps are the direct sources. Pars gives the 'part', capere gives the 'take'; both are old Latin words with reconstructed PIE roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 participare 与 particeps 是直接来源。pars 提供“部分”，capere 提供“拿取”；两者都是古老拉丁词，有重构的原始印欧语词根。

items.meaning: to take part or share in something
items.example: Everyone may participate.
items.exampleCN: 每个人都可以参与。

items.meaning: the act of taking part
items.example: Participation was higher than expected.
items.exampleCN: 参与度高于预期。

items.meaning: a person who takes part
items.example: Each participant received a form.
items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都收到一份表格。

items.meaning: organized so that people can take part
items.example: The project uses a participatory method.
items.exampleCN: 该项目采用参与式方法。

items.meaning: allowing or encouraging involvement, especially in management
items.meaningCN: 参与性的，尤指管理风格
items.example: Participative leadership raises trust.
items.exampleCN: 参与式领导提升信任。

items.meaning: not taking part; not sharing in profits
items.example: Nonparticipating shares carry no dividend.
items.exampleCN: 不参与分红的股份没有红利。

items.meaning: a portion of a whole
items.example: Each part has its own function.
items.exampleCN: 每一部分都有自己的功能。

items.meaning: to take or seize
items.example: The verb captures the idea of taking.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词抓住了“拿取”的意思。

items.meaning: taking part; in insurance, sharing in profits
items.example: A participating policy pays dividends.
items.exampleCN: 分红型保单支付红利。

latinEntries.meaning: to share, to take part in
latinEntries.example: Participare is the direct source of English participate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: participare 是英语 participate 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Particeps literally means taking a part.
latinEntries.exampleCN: particeps 字面意为“拿取一份”。

latinEntries.meaning: a part, a portion, a share
latinEntries.example: Pars is the base of portion and partial.
